 0 \rightarrow \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N) \rightarrow \mathcal{T}^R_0 \rightarrow C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0}) \rightarrow 0.
    \end{equation}
    Given $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and a homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable, split exact functor $F:\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathcal{D}$ taking values in the group objects of a semi-additive $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$, $F(A \otimes \mathcal{T}^R_0)\simeq 0$.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The existence of the semi-split extension readily follows from \Cref{prop: real toep extn} and the isomorphism of Real $C^*$-algebras
    \[
    C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0}) \cong \ker(C(\mathbb{S}^{1,1})\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{(0,1)}} \mathbb C).
    \]
    The second part of the corollary is proven just as in the complex case, see \cite[Section 6]{KKandE} and \cite[Corollary 1.5.3]{SCHROEDER}.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
\label{cor: loop eq cor}
    If $A$ is a group object in $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, then the component of $\beta_!$
    \[\beta_{!,A}: C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes_! A \rightarrow A\] is an equivalence.
<!-- end cor-4 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The proof of \cite[Corollary 6.11]{KKandE} will work with the obvious modifications.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- defi-11: body_md -->
\label{defi: KKRsep}
    Define $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ to be the Dwyer-Kan localization of $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ at $W_{\operatorname{Bott}}$, and denote by 
    \[
    L_{\operatorname{Bott}}: \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}
    \]
    the localization functor.
<!-- end defi-11 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop: imp}
    \hfill
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ is left-exact. $L_{\operatorname{Bott}}$ is also left-exact and has a fully faithful left-adjoint. $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ can be realized as the full subcategory of group objects of $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}$. 
        \item $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ is a small stable $\infty$-category. 
        \item $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ is countably cocomplete. For a countable collection $(B_n)_{n \in \mathbb N}$ of algebras in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, we have an equivalence
        \[
        \coprod_{n \in \mathbb N}\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}(B_n) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}(\oplus_{n \in \mathbb N} B_n) .
        \]
        When $!=\operatorname{ex}$, $\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ even preserves general countable filtered colimits. 
        \item Every left-exact functor from $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to a left-exact additive $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$ automatically factors (essentially uniquely) through $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$. More precisely, for every left-exact $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$, we have an equivalence
        \[
        \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lex}}(\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}) \xrightarrow[\simeq]{L_{\operatorname{Bott}}^*} \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lex}}(\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}).
        \]
        \item For every countably cocomplete stable $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$, we have an equivalence
        \[
        \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}_{\omega}}(\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}) \xrightarrow[\simeq]{{\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}^{*}} \mathbf{Fun}^{h,{\mathcal{K}_G},!,\oplus_\omega}(\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}),
        \]
        where the superscript $\operatorname{colim}_\omega$ denotes the full subcategory of functors which are countable colimit preserving.
        \item $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ has a symmetric monoidal refinement for both the tensor products when $!=\operatorname{se}$, and only for the maximal tensor product when $!=\operatorname{ex}$. 
        \item $L_{\operatorname{Bott}}$ has a symmetric monoidal refinement for the tensor product(s) on $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Consequently, the same assertions are true for $\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$. Moreover, the functors
        \[
        \otimes_?:\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}\times \mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}\rightarrow \mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}\] are bi-countable colimit preserving (for every choice of $(?,!)$ except $(\operatorname{min,ex})$).
\item For every left-exact symmetric monoidal additive $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$, pullback along the symmetric monoidal refinement(s) of $L_{\operatorname{Bott}}$  induces an equivalence
        \[
        \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lex}}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}(\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}) \xrightarrow[\simeq]{L_{\operatorname{Bott}}^*} \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lex}}_{\operatorname{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}
        }(\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}).
        \]
                \item For every symmetric monoidal countably cocomplete stable $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$, pullback along the symmetric monoidal refinement(s) of $\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$  induces an equivalence
        \[
        \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}_{\omega}}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}(\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}) \xrightarrow[\simeq]{{\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}^*} \mathbf{Fun}^{h,{\mathcal{K}_G},!,\oplus_\omega}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}(\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}).
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
We give some details in this proof as the result is ubiquitous for what we do later.\\\\
    Assertion $1$ follows directly from \Cref{eqn: red toep eqn} and the dual version of \cite[Proposition 5.2.7.4]{HTT}, as has been spelled out at the beginning of Section 7 in \cite{KKandE}.\\\\
    We now show Assertion 2. In light of \cite[Proposition 1.4.2.27]{HA}, it suffices to show $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ is small, pointed, left-exact and the loop functor on it is an equivalence. The first three properties are clear in light of Assertion 1 and the work done in the previous three subsections. It remains to see that loops is an equivalence. But this follows from \Cref{cor: loop eq cor} and the last part of Assertion 1.\\\\
    We now move onto Assertion 3. By \Cref{prop: SKGexcl omnibus}.1, $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ has countable coproducts, whence so does $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ being a Bousfield localization of it (see \cite[Subsection 7.1.4]{kerodon}). Any stable $\infty$-category having countable coproducts is automatically countably cocomplete. That countable coproducts in $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ are modeled by countable direct sum of the algebras follows from \Cref{prop: SKGexcl omnibus}.3 and because of general properties of (co)limits in a Bousfield localization; see again \cite[Subsection 7.1.4]{kerodon}. The case of $!=\operatorname{ex}$ is the content of \cite[Proposition 3.17]{EisCASS} (the Real structure poses no additional difficulty).\\\\
   Assertion 4 follows directly from \Cref{cor: real red toep extn} and \Cref{defi: KKRsep}. \\\\
    Assertion 5 is arguably the most important result from this section for us. It follows from the series of equivalences
    \[
    \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}_{\omega}}(\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}) \xrightarrow[\simeq]{L_{\operatorname{Bott}}^*} \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lex},\coprod_\omega}(\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}) \xrightarrow[\simeq]{L_{h,{\mathcal{K}_G},!,\oplus_\omega}^*}  \mathbf{Fun}^{{h,{\mathcal{K}_G},!+Sch,\oplus_\omega}}(\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D}),
    \]
    where the first equivalence follows from Assertion 4 and (the proof of) Assertion 3, and the second one is \Cref{uni prop excision iwthout symm mon}. We now conclude using \Cref{prop: automatic Schochet exactness}.\\\\
    Assertion 6 follows from \cite[Proposition 3.3.2]{HIN} and the basic permeance properties of $!$-exact sequences with respect to the minimal and maximal tensor products. \\\\
    The first two parts of Assertion 7 follow immediately from the nuclearity of $\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N),\mathcal{T}^R, C(\mathbb{S}^{1,1})$ and \cite[Proposition 3.3.2]{HIN}. For the final part, we use the fact that a left-exact and countable coproduct preserving functor between stable $\infty$-categories is automatically countable colimit preserving.\\\\
     For Assertion 8, we build the diagram 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathbf{Fun}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}^{\operatorname{lex}}(KK_{!,\operatorname{sep}}^{G,\infty},\mathcal{D})} && {\mathbf{Fun}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}^{\operatorname{lex}}(S_{\mathcal{K}_G}G\operatorname{\!-\!}C^*\operatorname{\!-alg}_{\operatorname{R,h,!,\oplus}_\omega}^{\operatorname{sep}},\mathcal{D})} \\
	{\mathbf{Fun}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}^{\operatorname{}}(KK_{!,\operatorname{sep}}^{G,\infty},\mathcal{D})} && {\mathbf{Fun}^{W_{\operatorname{Bott}}}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}(S_{\mathcal{K}_G}G\operatorname{\!-\!}C^*\operatorname{\!-alg}_{\operatorname{R,h,!,\oplus_\omega}}^{\operatorname{sep}},\mathcal{D})}
	\arrow["{L_{\operatorname{Bott}}^*}", dashed, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{L_{\operatorname{Bott}}^*,\simeq}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    The lower horizontal arrow is an equivalence from \Cref{defi: KKRsep} and \cite[Proposition 3.3.2]{HIN}. The dashed arrow can be seen to exist using the fact that $L_{\operatorname{Bott}}$ is left-exact. It remains to show that it is an equivalence. For that, we use the following general fact about symmetric monoidal left-exact Dwyer-Kan localizations: for any symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathcal{C}$ and an (essentially small) collection of morphisms $W \subseteq \mathcal{C}$ which are a tensor ideal in $\mathcal{C}$, if the Dwyer-Kan localization of $\mathcal{C}$ at $W$ is left-exact, then we have an equivalence
    \[
    \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lex}}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{C}[W^{-1}],\mathcal{E}) \xrightarrow[\simeq]{L_W^*} \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lex},W}_{\otimes_?/\operatorname{lax}}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{E})
    \]
    for every left-exact symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathcal{E}$. See \cite[Proposition 7.5.6]{CIS} for details.
    \\\\
    The proof of Assertion 9 follows in parallel to the proof of Assertion 5, in light of Assertion 8.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- cor-5: body_md -->
\label{cor: s fib seqn}
    \hfill
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item In $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$, we have an equivalence $qA \xrightarrow{\simeq} A$ for all $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.
        \item The fiber sequence 
        \[
        \mathcal{S} \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_0} \mathbb C \xrightarrow{\iota} Cl^{0,1}
        \]
        in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ as discussed in \Cref{prop: S to C to Cl fib seqn in homotopy cat} remains a fiber sequence in $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G_2,\mathrm{sep}}$.
        \item The composite
\[
(\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u \xrightarrow{{\operatorname{ev}_0}_*} Cl^{0,1}_u \xrightarrow{\pi_1} \mathbb C
\]
is an equivalence in $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-5 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Assertion 1 is the content of \cite[Lemma 11.4]{KKandE}, the generalization to the equivariant case is routine. Assertion 2 follows directly from \Cref{prop: S to C to Cl fib seqn in homotopy cat}, since we have shown before that each of the localizations in \Cref{eqn: kk functor} after $L_h$ are left-exact. Assertion 3 follows from Assertion 1 in light of the function algebra model of $q\mathbb C$ as described in \Cref{rem: qA properties}.4.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- rem-8: body_md -->
We present a more direct proof of \Cref{cor: s fib seqn}.3 in this remark. Consider the ladder of semi-split exact sequences in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\[
\footnotesize
\begin{tikzcd}
	0 & {\{f\in C_0((0,1],M_2(\mathbb{C})) \mid f(1) ~\text{dia}\}} & \begin{array}{c} \{f\in C([0,1],M_2(\mathbb{C})) \mid f(0)=\begin{psmallmatrix} * & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{psmallmatrix} ~\&~f(1) \text{dia}\} \end{array} & {\mathbb{C}} & 0 \\
	0 & {\mathbb{C}} & {\mathbb{C} \oplus \mathbb{C}} & {\mathbb{C}} & 0
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{inc}}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{(\operatorname{ev}_1)_{(1,1)}}"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{(\operatorname{ev}_0)_{(1,1)}}", from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{(\operatorname{ev}_0)_{(1,1)} \oplus (\operatorname{ev}_1)_{(1,1)}}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{id}}", no head, from=1-4, to=2-4]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\iota_2}", from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_1}", from=2-3, to=2-4]
	\arrow[from=2-4, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}\]
We have to show that the left vertical arrow is an equivalence in $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$. This will follow once the other two vertical arrows are shown to be equivalences in $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$. Only the case of the middle vertical arrow needs an argument. The fiber of 
\[
\{f\in C([0,1],M_2(\mathbb{C})) \mid f(0)=\begin{psmallmatrix} * & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{psmallmatrix} ~\&~f(1) ~\text{dia}\} \xrightarrow{(\operatorname{ev}_0)_{1,1} \oplus (\operatorname{ev}_1)_{1,1}} \mathbb C \oplus \mathbb C
\]
is readily seen to be the mapping cone of the right lower corner inclusion $\mathbb C \rightarrow M_2(\mathbb C)$, and hence is contractible in $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.
<!-- end rem-8 -->
<!-- defi-12: body_md -->
Denote by $W_{\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}$ the collection of morphisms inverted by the functor \[\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}.\]
<!-- end defi-12 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{prop: uni prop hoKK one categorical}{(cf. \cite[Proposition 13.13]{KKandE})}
    Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a half exact additive $1$-category with countable coproducts. Let $F: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathcal{D}$ be a functor which is homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable, half exact with respect to $!$-exact sequences, takes countable direct sums in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to countable coproducts in $\mathcal{D}$, and \emph{suspension stable} (i.e. for every morphism $f: A \rightarrow B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, $F(f)$ is an isomorphism if and only if $F(\Omega(f))$ is an isomorphism). Then $F$ inverts $W_{\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}$.
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Since $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ by construction is a series of Dwyer-Kan localizations of $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, we need to show that we can construct factorizations as indicated by the dashed arrows below
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: factorizations in one category}\begin{tikzcd}
\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}
&&
\\
\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}
&&
\mathcal{D}
\\
\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}
\\
\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}
 
\arrow["{L_{h,{\mathcal{K}_G}}}", from=1-1, to=2-1]
\arrow["F", from=1-1, to=2-3]
 
\arrow["{F'}"{description}, dashed, from=2-1, to=2-3]
\arrow["{L_{!,\oplus_\omega}}", from=2-1, to=3-1]
 
\arrow["{F''}"{description}, dashed, from=3-1, to=2-3]
\arrow["{L_{\mathrm{Bott}}}", from=3-1, to=4-1]
 
\arrow["{F'''}"{description}, dashed, from=4-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
    The first two hypothesis on $F$ yields the functor $F'$. Note that $F'$ inverts $\hat{W}_!$, as follows from \cite[Theorem 21.4.4]{BLAK} (which states that $F$ yields natural long exact sequences) and a standard 5-lemma argument applied to \Cref{eqn: excision diagram}.

    We now claim that $F'$ also inverts the closure $W_!$ of $\hat{W}_!$ under 2-out-of-3, pullbacks, and countable sums. It suffices to show that the collection of morphisms inverted by $F'$ is closed under pullbacks and countable sums. The argument for pullbacks can be extracted verbatim from the proof of the analogous assertion in \cite[Proposition 13.13]{KKandE}. That the collection of morphisms inverted by $F'$ are preserved under countable sums follows immediately from our hypothesis that the natural map \[\coprod_{n \in \mathbb N} F(A_n) \xrightarrow{}F(\oplus_{n \in \mathbb N} A_n)\]
    is an isomorphism. Thus, we deduce the existence of $F''$.

    The argument for $F''$ inverting the maps $\beta_{!,B}$ can be read off from the analogous step in the proof of \cite[Proposition 13.13]{KKandE} (with the obvious changes to the Toeplitz extension in the Real case as discussed in Subsection 3.4). This shows the existence of $F'''$ and the proof is complete.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- defi-13: body_md -->
\label{defi: change of groups}
    Let $H,G$ be locally compact, second countable groups.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item  Let $\varphi: H \rightarrow G$ be a continuous homomorphism\footnote{\emph{not necessarily} inclusion of a subgroup}. Then we have the obvious restriction functor
        \[
        \operatorname{res}^G_H: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathsf H\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}.
        \]
        \item When $H \subseteq G$ is closed, we define the induction functor
        \[
        \operatorname{ind}^G_H: \mathsf H\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}
        \]
        as follows:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item On objects, $\operatorname{ind}^G_H$ sends $B \in \mathsf H\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to the invariant $C^*$-subalgebra of $C_b(G,B)$ (the group $G$ acts on $C_b(G,B)$ by $(g,f) \longmapsto (g' \mapsto f(g^{-1}g'))$; note that this action is not neccesarily continuous, but it will be so on $\operatorname{ind}^G_H(B)$) generated by the functions $f:G \rightarrow B$ satisfying 
            \[
            f(gh)=h^{-1}f(g)~\forall h \in H,\forall g \in G~~\&~~\text{projection of}~\operatorname{supp}(f)~\text{to}~G/H~\text{is compact}.
            \]
            \item On morphisms, $\operatorname{ind}^G_H$ sends a morphism $\varphi: B \rightarrow B'$ in $\mathsf H\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to \[\operatorname{ind}^G_H(\varphi):\operatorname{ind}^G_H(B) \rightarrow \operatorname{ind}^G_H(B')\] given by $(\operatorname{ind}^G_H(\varphi)(f))(g):=\varphi(f(g))$.
        \end{itemize}
        \item When $H \subseteq G$ is closed and $G/H$ is compact, then we also call the associated induction functor as the  coinduction functor, and is denoted by $\mathsf{coind}^G_H$.\footnote{the coinduction functor can be defined under more general conditions, but we do not have any reason to do so.}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end defi-13 -->
<!-- rem-9: body_md -->
Note that $\operatorname{res}^G$ denotes the underlying non-equivariant $C^*$-algebra functor, and $\operatorname{res}_G$ denotes the functor which equips a (non-equivariant) $C^*$-algebra with the trivial $G$-action (we usually omit the trivial group from the notation). Similar comment also applies to the functors $\operatorname{res}^{G_2}_{C_2}$ and $\operatorname{res}^{C_2}_{G_2}$.
<!-- end rem-9 -->
<!-- prop-12: body_md -->
\label{prop: functors descend}
    All the functors defined above descend essentially uniquely to the respective equivariant $KK_{!,\infty}^{\operatorname{sep}}$-categories. Furthermore, the descended functors preserve countable colimits.
<!-- end prop-12 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
This can be extracted from \cite[Section 4]{BEL} and \cite[Section 2.1]{BUNKEcrossed}; no comparison with classical bivariant $K$-theories is made in loc.\! cit.\! to show that the functors descend, and the proof therein is based on universal properties which we have enforced by construction. Note that the last assertion follows from the universal property of the equivariant $KK_{!,\infty}^{\operatorname{sep}}$-category as described in \Cref{prop: imp}.5.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- rem-10: body_md -->
Note that the restriction functor has a symmetric monoidal refinement for every choice of $(?,!)$ except $(?,!)=(\min,\operatorname{ex})$, see \cite[Corollary 4.8]{BEL}. The same is not true for the induction or coinduction functors, as can be seen by looking at the unit.
<!-- end rem-10 -->
<!-- prop-13: body_md -->
\label{prop: adjunctions at skg level}
    If $H\subseteq G$ is open\footnote{recall that open subgroups of topological groups are automatically closed}, then we have an adjunction
    \[
\operatorname{ind}^G_H:
\mathsf S_{\mathcal K_H}\mathsf H\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_h^{\mathrm{sep}}
\;\leftrightarrows\;
\mathsf S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_h^{\mathrm{sep}}
:\operatorname{res}^G_H.
\]
<!-- end prop-13 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
We begin by the description of the unit and the co-unit.

    The unit will be the natural transformation
    $
        \varepsilon: \operatorname{id} \rightarrow \mathsf{res}^G_H \circ \mathsf{ind}^G_H
    $ with \begin{align*}
        \varepsilon_A: A &\rightarrow \mathsf{res}^G_H \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) \\
        a &\mapsto \chi_H(g)\alpha_{g^{-1}}a = \begin{cases}
            \alpha_{g^{-1}}a&\text{if}~g \in H \\
            0 &\text{otherwise}
        \end{cases}
    \end{align*}\footnote{this is just notation. $A$ is a $H$-$C^*$-algebra, so the action by a general element $g^{-1}$ in $G$ doesn't make sense. However, this will only be considered when $g^{-1} \in H$.}

    The description of the co-unit $\eta:\mathsf{ind}^G_H \circ \mathsf{res}^G_H \rightarrow \operatorname{id}$ is more complicated. It is easy to see that
    \[
    \mathsf{ind}^G_H (\mathsf{res}^G_H (B)) \cong C_0(G/H) \otimes B
    \]
    Upon representing $C_0(G/H)$ in $\mathcal{B}(L^2(G/H))$ as multiplication operators, $C_0(G/H)$ factors through $\mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H))$ since $G/H$ is discrete, courtesy $H$ being open in $G$. We can now define the co-unit maps by 
    \[
    \eta_B:\mathsf{ind}^G_H(\mathsf{res}^G_H(B)) \cong C_0(G/H) \otimes B \rightarrow \mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H)) \otimes B \simeq B.
    \]
    It remains to check the triangle identities. We have that the composite
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{res}^G_H&(B) \xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{\mathsf{res}^G_H(B)}} \mathsf{res}^G_H(\mathsf{ind}^G_H(\mathsf{res}^G_H(B))) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{res}^G_H(\eta_B)} \mathsf{res}^G_H(B)
    \end{align*}
    maps
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{res}^G_H(B) \ni b &\longmapsto g\mapsto\chi_H(g)\beta_{g^{-1}}(b) \\
        &\longmapsto gH\mapsto\chi_H(g)\beta_g\beta_{g^{-1}}(b) \\
        &= gH \mapsto \chi_H(g)b \\
        &\longmapsto \chi_H \otimes b \in \mathsf{res}^G_H(\mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H))\otimes B) \\
        &\longmapsfrom b,
    \end{align*}
    where the last map is a left-upper corner inclusion. Note that as a $H$-$C^*$-algebra, $\mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H))$ has the trivial action. It follows that \[
    \mathsf{res}^G_H(\eta_B) \circ \varepsilon_{\mathsf{res}^G_H(B)} \simeq \operatorname{id}_{\mathsf{res}^G_H(B)}.
    \]
    The analysis of the other composite is more subtle. We have that the composite
    \[
    \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{ind}^G_H(\varepsilon_A)} \mathsf{ind}^G_H(\mathsf{res}^G_H(\mathsf{ind}^G_H(A))) \xrightarrow{\eta_{\mathsf{ind}^G_H(A)} } \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A)
    \]
    maps
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) \ni (g \mapsto f(g)) &\quad \longmapsto (g \mapsto (l \mapsto \chi_H(l)\alpha_{l^{-1}}f(g))) \in \mathsf{ind}^G_H(\mathsf{res}^G_H(\mathsf{ind}^G_H(A))) \\ 
        &\quad \longmapsto (gH \mapsto (l \mapsto \chi_H(g^{-1}l)\alpha_{(g^{-1}l)^{-1}}f(g)))\in C_0(G/H,\operatorname{ind}^G_H(A)) \\
        &\quad = (gH \mapsto (l \mapsto \chi_H(g^{-1}l)f(l)))\in C_0(G/H,\operatorname{ind}^G_H(A)) \\
        &\quad \xmapsto{(\dagger)} \sum_{kH \in G/H} \chi_{kH} \otimes \chi_{kH}f \in \mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H)) \otimes \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) ~\text{(see \Cref{lem: technical manipulation} below)}
    \end{align*}
    It remains to analyse the fate of $\sum_{kH \in G/H} \chi_{kH} \otimes \chi_{kH}f$ under the equivalences 
    \[
    \mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H)) \otimes \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H)) \otimes \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) \xleftarrow{\simeq} \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A).
    \]
    We will be done if we can prove the following
    \begin{clm}
        The two homomorphisms $\mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) \rightarrow \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H)) \otimes \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A)$ given by \[f \mapsto \sum_{kH \in G/H} \chi_{kH} \otimes \chi_{kH}f\] and \[f \mapsto p \otimes f\] are homotopic, where $p\in \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H))$ is the projection onto the summand $\mathbb C$.
    \end{clm}
    \begin{proof}
        Let $i:\mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H)) \xrightarrow{} \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H)) $ denote the embedding. Then, $i(\chi_{kH}) \in \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H))$ is a (not $G$-equivariant) one-dimensional projection. It is elementary to see that there is a rank-one partial isometry $u \in \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H))$ such that $upu^*=i(\chi_{eH})$. Defining $u_k:=ku$, we also have $u_kpu_k^*=i(\chi_{kH})$. Our sought after homotopy is then given by the following one-parameter family of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms
        \begin{align*}
            \varphi_t:\mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) &\rightarrow \mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H)) \otimes \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A)\\ \quad 
            f &\mapsto \underset{kH \in G/H}{\Sigma} (\cos(\frac{\pi}{2}t)^2i(\chi_{kH}) 
            +\sin(\frac{\pi}{2}t)^2p+\cos(\frac{\pi}{2}t)\sin(\frac{\pi}{2}t)(u_k+u_k^*)) \otimes \chi_{kH}f.
        \end{align*}
    \end{proof}
    This finishes the proof of the proposition.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- clm-1: body_md -->
The two homomorphisms $\mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) \rightarrow \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H)) \otimes \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A)$ given by \[f \mapsto \sum_{kH \in G/H} \chi_{kH} \otimes \chi_{kH}f\] and \[f \mapsto p \otimes f\] are homotopic, where $p\in \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H))$ is the projection onto the summand $\mathbb C$.
<!-- end clm-1 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Let $i:\mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H)) \xrightarrow{} \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H)) $ denote the embedding. Then, $i(\chi_{kH}) \in \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H))$ is a (not $G$-equivariant) one-dimensional projection. It is elementary to see that there is a rank-one partial isometry $u \in \mathcal{K}(\mathbb C \oplus L^2(G/H))$ such that $upu^*=i(\chi_{eH})$. Defining $u_k:=ku$, we also have $u_kpu_k^*=i(\chi_{kH})$. Our sought after homotopy is then given by the following one-parameter family of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms
        \begin{align*}
            \varphi_t:\mathsf{ind}^G_H(A) &\rightarrow \mathcal{K}(L^2(G/H)) \otimes \mathsf{ind}^G_H(A)\\ \quad 
            f &\mapsto \underset{kH \in G/H}{\Sigma} (\cos(\frac{\pi}{2}t)^2i(\chi_{kH}) 
            +\sin(\frac{\pi}{2}t)^2p+\cos(\frac{\pi}{2}t)\sin(\frac{\pi}{2}t)(u_k+u_k^*)) \otimes \chi_{kH}f.
        \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- rem-11: body_md -->
\label{lem: technical manipulation}
    We give here details of the map labelled $(\dagger)$ in the last proof.

    On the one hand, we have 
    \begin{align*}
        gH \longmapsto& (l \mapsto \chi_H(g^{-1}l)f(l))
        =(l \mapsto \chi_{gH}(l)f(l))
    \end{align*}
    On the other hand, under the identification $C_0(G/H) \otimes \operatorname{ind}^G_H(A) \cong C_0(G/H,\operatorname{ind}^G_H(A))$, we have \[\underset{{kH \in G/H}}{\sum} \chi_{kH} \otimes \chi_{kH}f\] corresponds to the map
    \begin{align*}
        gH \longmapsto (l \mapsto \underset{kH \in G/H}{\sum}\chi_{kH}(g).\chi_{kH}(l)f(l)).
    \end{align*}
    On a fixed $gH \in G/H$, both the functions take the value $f(l)$ if $l \in gH$, and $0$ otherwise.
<!-- end rem-11 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm: adjunctions at kkg}
     Let $H\subseteq G$ be open. Then we have an adjunction
    \[
\operatorname{ind}^G_H:
\mathrm{KK}^{H,\mathrm{sep}}_{!,\infty}
\;\leftrightarrows\;
\mathrm{KK}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{!,\infty}
:\operatorname{res}^G_H.
\]
    Let $H \subseteq G$ be closed and $G/H$ be compact. Then we have an adjunction
    \[
\operatorname{res}^G_H:
\mathrm{KK}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{!,\infty}
\;\leftrightarrows\;
\mathrm{KK}^{H,\mathrm{sep}}_{!,\infty}
:\mathsf{coind}^G_H.
\]
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
The first statement follows directly from \Cref{prop: functors descend} and \Cref{prop: adjunctions at skg level}, since adjunctions descend to a Dwyer-Kan localization if functors do.

    The second statement also follows from \Cref{prop: functors descend} since we have already have an adjunction 
     \[
\operatorname{res}^G_H:
\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}
\;\leftrightarrows\;
\mathsf H\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}
:\mathsf{coind}^G_H.
\]
    at the level of algebras (see \cite[Lemma 4.2]{BDS}). For our ease of reference later, we mention the unit and counit of this adjunction here:
    \begin{align*}
        \eta_A: &A \rightarrow \mathsf{coind}^G_H\mathsf{res}^G_H(A),~~a \mapsto \eta(a):=(G \ni t \mapsto ta \in A) \\
    \epsilon_B:&\mathsf{res}^G_H\mathsf{coind}^G_H(B) \rightarrow B,~~f \mapsto \epsilon_B(f):=f(1).
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- defi-14: body_md -->
\label{defi: special}
    $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is called \emph{$!$-special} if it satisfies the following three conditions\footnote{The H in the enumeration below stands for Hypothesis!}.
    \begin{enumerate}[{(H1)}]
        \item For any $!$-exact sequence $0 \rightarrow B \rightarrow C \rightarrow D \rightarrow 0$ in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, the induced map 
        \[\operatorname{Map}_{\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}}(A,B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}) \rightarrow \operatorname{Map}_{\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}}(A,C \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}) \rightarrow \operatorname{Map}_{\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}}(A,D \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}) 
        \]
        is a fiber sequence in Anima.
        \item The natural map of abelian monoids
        \[
        \oplus_{n \in \mathbb N}[A,B_n \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]_G \rightarrow[A,\oplus_{n \in \mathbb N} (B_n \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G})]_G 
        \]
        is an isomorphism for all countable collection of algebras $\{B_n\}_{n \in \mathbb N}$ in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.
        \item The abelian monoid of stable $G$-homotopy classes of maps $[A,B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]_G$ is a group for all $B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end defi-14 -->
<!-- rem-12: body_md -->
\label{rem: special sufficient}
    Clearly, $\operatorname{ex-special} \implies \operatorname{se-special}$. In the algebras we consider, we will be showing that they are $\operatorname{ex-special}$.
    
    H1 will be satisfied if the induced map of topological spaces
    \[
    \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_G(A,B) \rightarrow \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_G(A,C) \rightarrow \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_G(A,D)
    \]
    is a Serre fibration of topological spaces for every $!$-exact sequence $0 \rightarrow B \rightarrow C \rightarrow D \rightarrow 0$. Indeed, this follows since $- \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}$ is an exact functor on $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and because the $\infty$-category $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is presented by the topologically enriched category $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$; see \Cref{prop: RALGseph omnibus}.1.

    Similarly, a sufficient criterion to check H2 is that the functor 
    \[
    [A,-]_G: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \operatorname{Set}
    \]
    preserves countable filtered colimits. This is because countable direct sums can be written as a filtered colimit of finite direct sums, and the functor $[A,-]_G$ clearly preserves finite direct sums of algebras in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.
<!-- end rem-12 -->
<!-- prop-14: body_md -->
\label{prop: special consequences}
    If $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is $\operatorname{!-special}$, then 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The functor
        \[
        \operatorname{map}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}}(A,-): \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathbf{CMon}(\operatorname{An})
        \]
        takes values in $\mathbf{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})$.
        \item The functor
        \[
        F_A:=\operatorname{map}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}}(A,-): \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathbf{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})
        \]
        factors through $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ (necessarily essentially uniquely) as the functor
        \[
        \tau_{\geq 0}\operatorname{map}_{\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}(A,-): \mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}\rightarrow \mathbf{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})
        \]
        \item For each $B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, there exists a natural equivalence in $\mathbf{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})$
        \[
        \operatorname{map}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}}(A,B) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \tau_{\geq 0}\operatorname{map}_{\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}(A,B)
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-14 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Assertion 1 is an immediate consequence of H3 and the fact that being a commutative group is a \emph{property} of a commutative monoid which is furthermore tested on $\pi_0$.\\\\
    To show Assertion 2, we first show that we have a factorization of $F_A$ as indicated by the dashed arrows below.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}} & {} && {\mathbf{CGrp}(\operatorname{An})} \\
	{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus}^{\mathrm{sep}}} \\
	{\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}
	\arrow["{F_A}", from=1-1, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{L_{!,\oplus_\omega}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{F_A'}"{pos=0.3}, dashed, from=2-1, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{L_{\mathrm{Bott}}}"', from=2-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{F_A''}"{pos=0.4}, dashed, from=3-1, to=1-4]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
    To see that $F_A'$ exists, we bring \Cref{prop: SKGexcl omnibus}.3 into play. We need to check that $F_A$ is left-exact, inverts $\hat{W}_!$ and preserves countable coproducts. Being a corepresentable functor, $F_A$ is clearly left-exact. That it inverts $\hat{W}_!$ follows directly from H1 in presence of \Cref{eqn: excision diagram}. That $F_A$ also preserves countable coproducts is a consequence of H2, as can be seen from the Whitehead's theorem for spectra together with the fact that filtered colimits of spectra commute with finite limits. 
             
                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                
                                                                                                                                                                    
   
    To now see that $F_A''$ exists, we simply use \Cref{prop: imp}.4.
    
    That the factorizations $F_A'$ and $F_A''$ are essentially unique follows from the fact that $L_{!,\oplus_\omega}$ and $L_{\operatorname{Bott}}$ are Dwyer-Kan localizations. That $F_A'$ and $F_A''$ are also corepresentable by $A$ follows since the left-Kan extension of a corepresentable functor is corepresentable (\cite[Corollary 8.3.1.9]{kerodon}), and in our case, $F_A'$ and $F_A''$ are also left-Kan extensions of $F_A$ along the localization maps. \\\\
    Assertion 3 also follows from the previous paragraph.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- cor-6: body_md -->
\label{cor: special mapping spaces in KK}
    For any $!$-special algebra $A$ and any $B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, we have an weak homotopy equivalence of spaces
    \[
    \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_G(A,B \otimes \mathcal{K}_G) \simeq \Omega^{
    \infty
    }\operatorname{map}_{\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}(A,B).
    \]
    Moreover, under the above equivalence, the block-sum addition on $[A,B \otimes \mathcal{K}_G]_G$ coincides with the additive structure on $\pi_0(\operatorname{map}_{\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}(A,B))$.
<!-- end cor-6 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem: s special}
    $\mathcal{S} \in \mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is $\operatorname{ex-special}$.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
The necessary verifications are the content of the first three assertions of \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}. Note that we are implicitly using that the $C^*$-algebra of compact operators on a Hilbert space is inner graded.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem: qC special}
    $q\mathbb C \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is $\operatorname{ex-special}$.
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
That $q\mathbb C$ satisfies H3 follows from the fact that $[q\mathbb C,B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]_G$ is naturally isomorphic to the abelian group $K^G_0(B)$. Since $K^G_0(-)$ is known to preserve filtered colimits (for example, by combining Assertion 3 and Assertion 6 of \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}), $q\mathbb C$ also satisfies H2.
    
    That $q\mathbb C$ satisfies H1 can be shown directly, but we instead deduce it from \Cref{lem: s special}. To that end, we leverage the isomorphism of $C^*$-algebras $q\mathbb C \cong (\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u$ as mentioned in \Cref{rem: qA properties}.5. The rest follows from the fact that $\mathcal{S}$ satisfies H1 for the group $G_2$ and the restriction-coinduction adjunction. In more detail, for any $B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, we have natural equivalences
   \[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}(q\mathbb C,B)
&\simeq
\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}\!\left(
\mathsf{res}^{G_2}_{G}(\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}),B
\right)
\\
&\simeq
\mathsf S_{\mathcal K_{G_2}}
\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_h^{\mathrm{sep}}
\!\left(
\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1},
B\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}
\right)
\\
&\xrightarrow[\simeq]{\hat\otimes Cl^{1,0}}
\mathsf S_{\mathcal K_{G_2}}
\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_h^{\mathrm{sep}}(\mathcal{S},B).
\end{aligned}
\]
    Note that for the second equivalence, we are using the identification\footnote{the more well known isomorphism is with the ungraded tensor product, but since $B$ has the trivial $C_2$-action, we can also use the graded tensor product.} $\mathsf{coind}^{G_2}_G B \cong B \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}$. For the final equivalence, we are also using that the graded tensor products $\hat\otimes_!$ on $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ also descend to a symmetric monoidal structure on $\mathsf S_{\mathcal K_{G_2}}
\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_h^{\mathrm{sep}}$, which is easy to see since the algebras of continuous functions on the unit interval and compact operators on a Hilbert space are inner graded.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- rem-13: body_md -->
We note that $\mathbb C$ is \emph{not} $!$-special, as H3 fails for it. We mention without proof that $C_0(\mathbb R^{0,1})$ is $!$-special.
<!-- end rem-13 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat}
    We have natural equivalences of spaces for any \(B\in\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(\hat B\in\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}\):
\[
\mathbb K^{G}(B)
\simeq
\Omega^{\infty}\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}(\mathbb C,B),
\qquad
\mathbb{\hat K}^{G}(\hat B)
\simeq
\Omega^{\infty}\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G_2,\mathrm{sep}}(\mathcal{S},\hat B).
\]
    Moreover, $K_0^G(-), \mathrm{KK}_{!,0}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}(\mathbb C,-): \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}$ are equivalent as lax monoidal functors, where $\mathrm{KK}_{!,0}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}(\mathbb C,-)$ denotes the homotopy category of $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$.
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
The first two assertions follow from \Cref{cor: special mapping spaces in KK} and the last two lemmas. For the first assertion we are also using that $q\mathbb C$ and $\mathbb C$ are equivalent in $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$, as follows from \Cref{cor: s fib seqn}.1. The last assertion follows from the lax case of \Cref{prop: imp}.9.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- defi-15: body_md -->
Denote by 
    \[
    \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}:=\operatorname{Ind}_{\aleph_1}(\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}),
    \]
    where $\operatorname{Ind}_{\aleph_1}(\mathcal{C})$ denotes the $\aleph_1$-ind completion of $\mathcal{C}$, i.e. the category obtained by \emph{freely adding}\footnote{see \cite[Proposition 5.3.5.10]{HTT} for the precise universal property} $\aleph_1$-filtered colimits to $\mathcal{C}$. We define functors
    \[
    \mathrm{kk}^{G}_{!,\infty}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}
    \]
    as left Kan-extensions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}} && {\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}} & {\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}} \\
	&& {\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}}
	\arrow["{\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{incl.}}"', from=1-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["y", from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{!,\infty}}"'{pos=0.6}, dashed, from=2-3, to=1-4]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
where $y: \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ind}_{\aleph_1}(\mathcal{C})$ denotes the canonical embedding (which preserves countable filtered colimits by \cite[Proposition 5.3.5.14]{HTT}).
<!-- end defi-15 -->
<!-- defi-16: body_md -->
\label{defi: s finitary}
    A functor $F$ defined on $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$ is called \emph{s-finitary} if for every $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$, the canonical map 
    \[
    \operatorname{colim}_{A' \subseteq_{\operatorname{sep}}A} F(A') \rightarrow F(A)
    \]
    is an equivalence, where $A'$ runs through the separable $G$-invariant $C^*$-subalgebras of $A$.
<!-- end defi-16 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem: s finitary}
    Let $F:\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \rightarrow \mathcal{D}$ be a functor to an $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$ having all small filtered colimits. We have a canonical natural transformation $c: \hat{F} \implies F$, where $\hat{F}$ is the left Kan extension of $F\mid_{\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}}$. Then the functor $F$ is s-finitary if and only if $c$ is an equivalence.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
This follows immediately from the pointwise formula for left Kan extension, and the fact that every morphism $A \rightarrow B$ in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$ with $A$ separable factors through a $G$-invariant separable $C^*$-subalgebra of $B$. See \cite[Lemma 3.1]{BEL} for more details.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- prop-15: body_md -->
\label{prop: ind omnibus}
    \hfill
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The category $\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ is a presentably symmetric monoidal (for every choice of $(?,!)$ except $(\min,\operatorname{ex})$), stable $\infty$-category, and $\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ can be identified with the full subcategory of $\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ comprising of $\aleph_1$-compact objects.
        \item The functor $\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{!,\infty}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ is symmetric monoidal (for every choice of $(?,!)$ except $(\min,\operatorname{ex})$), homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable, $!$-exact, preserves countable direct sums and is s-finitary\footnote{note that any functor on $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$ which preserves countable direct sums and is s-finitary automatically preserves all direct sums.}.
        \item Pullback along $\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ induces for every cocomplete symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}$ with bi-cocontinous tensor product an equivalence
        \[
        (\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{!,\infty})^*: \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}_{\otimes_?\operatorname{/lax}}(\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty},\mathcal{D}) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \mathbf{Fun}^{h,{\mathcal{K}_G},\operatorname{!},\oplus_\omega,\operatorname{sfin}}_{\otimes_?\operatorname{/lax}}(\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg},\mathcal{D}),
        \]
        where the superscript $\operatorname{sfin}$ denotes s-finitary functors.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-15 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Assertion 1 follows from the general fact that if $\mathcal{C}$ is a small, symmetric monoidal, $\kappa$-cocomplete (for some regular cardinal $\kappa$), stable $\infty$-category such that the tensor product preserves $\kappa$-small colimits in each variable, then $\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})$ is a presentably symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category and $\mathcal{C}$ can be identified with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Ind}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{C})$ comprising of $\aleph_1$-compact objects. See \cite[Theorem 5.5.1.1]{HTT}, \cite[Proposition 1.1.3.6]{HA} and \cite[Corollary 4.8.1.14]{HA}.\\\\
       The proof of Assertion 2 can be taken from \cite[Theorem 1.18]{BEL} and \cite[Proposition 3.8]{BEL}\footnote{the proof of lax monoidality of $\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ is formal, but to show its (strong) monoidality, one has to look into the structure of the minimal and maximal tensor products; see loc.\! cit.\! for details}. Note that although \cite{BEL} is written with $\operatorname{Ind}_{\aleph_0}$-completion, all the filtered diagrams considered in Section 3 of loc.\! cit.\! are indeed $\aleph_1$-filtered, and so the proofs go through in our context too. The Real and the (potentially) non-discrete group case do not pose any difficulties.\\\\
       Assertion 3 follows from the series of equivalences
       \[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}}_{\otimes_?\operatorname{/lax}}
    (\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty},\mathcal{D})
&\xrightarrow[\simeq]{y^*}
\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{colim}_{\omega}}_{\otimes_?\operatorname{/lax}}
    (\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D})
\\[0.6em]
&\xrightarrow[\simeq]{{\mathrm{kk}_{!,\infty}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}^*}
\mathbf{Fun}^{h,{\mathcal{K}_G},!,\oplus_\omega}_{\otimes_?\operatorname{/lax}}
    (\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}},\mathcal{D})
\\
&\xleftarrow[\simeq]{\operatorname{incl}^*}
\mathbf{Fun}^{h,{\mathcal{K}_G},!,\oplus_\omega,\operatorname{sfin}}_
    {\otimes_?\operatorname{/lax}}
    (\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg},\mathcal{D}).
\end{aligned}
\]
       where the first equivalence follows from \cite[Proposition 5.3.5.10]{HTT} and \cite[Corollary 4.8.1.14]{HA}, the second equivalence is the content of \Cref{prop: imp}.9, and the last equivalence follows from \Cref{lem: s finitary} and Assertion 2. Note that the inverse to the last equivalence is precisely the left Kan-extension along the inclusion $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \xrightarrow{\operatorname{incl.}} \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}
     We have natural equivalences of spaces for any \(B\in\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}\) and \(\hat{B}\in\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}\):
\[
\mathbb{K}^{G}(B)
\simeq
\Omega^{\infty}\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}(\mathbb C,B),
\qquad
\mathbb{\hat K}^G(\hat{B})
\simeq
\Omega^{\infty}\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(\mathcal{S},\hat{B}).
\]
    Moreover, $K_0^G(-), \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,0}(\mathbb C,-): \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}$ {are equivalent as lax monoidal functors, where $\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,0}$ denotes the homotopy category of $\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}$.}
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
This follows immediately from \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat} upon noting that all the relevant functors preserve $\aleph_1$-filtered colimits.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- cor-7: body_md -->
\label{cor: EC2 SS ring}
        $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,0}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}) \cong \frac{\mathbb Z[x]}{x^2=1}$ as rings, with the preferred isomorphism mapping $[\operatorname{1}_{\mathcal{S}}]$ to $1$, and $[\alpha_\mathcal{S}]$ to $x$. For any graded $C^*$-algebra $A$, the action of $\alpha_A$ on $\hat{K}_0(A)$ coincides with the action of $\alpha_\mathcal{S} \in \mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,0}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S})$ on $\hat{K}_0(A)$ stemming from the product in the  $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,0}$ category.
<!-- end cor-7 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
This is immediate from Assertion 8 of \Cref{prop: omnibus graded k-theory} and \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- rem-14: body_md -->
\label{rem: C2 action on graded k theory}
        The second perspective in \Cref{cor: EC2 SS ring} directly shows why even the boundary maps in the long exact sequences of graded $K$-theory groups preserve the action of the grading (and this is because of the associativity of composition in the $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,0}$ category), and hence the associated long exact sequence can be viewed as a long exact sequence of $C_2$-abelian groups.
<!-- end rem-14 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{thm: change of group general}
    There are obvious analogues of the change of group functors of \Cref{defi: change of groups} to the categories of all $C^*$-algebras. These functors then descend to cocontinuous functors between the respective equivariant $KK_{!,\infty}$-categories. The restriction functors have symmetric monoidal refinement for every choice of $(?,!)$ except for $(\min,\operatorname{ex})$. If \(H\subseteq G\) is open, then we have an adjunction
\[
\operatorname{ind}^G_H:
\mathrm{KK}^{H}_{!,\infty}
\leftrightarrows
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}
:
\operatorname{res}^G_H.
\]

If \(H\subseteq G\) is closed and \(G/H\) is compact, then we have an adjunction
\[
\operatorname{res}^G_H:
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}
\leftrightarrows
\mathrm{KK}^{H}_{!,\infty}
:
\mathsf{coind}^G_H.
\]
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
In light of the results of Section 3.5 and \Cref{prop: ind omnibus}.3, we have to show that the functors $\mathsf{ind}^{G}_H(-),\mathsf{res}^G_H(-), \mathsf{coind}^G_H(-)$ between the relevant categories of all $C^*$-algebras are s-finitary. But this is contained in \cite[Section 4]{BEL}, see also \cite[Section 2.1]{BUNKEcrossed}.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- prop-16: body_md -->
\label{prop: dia on s}
    There is a unique graded $*$-homomorphism $\mathcal{S} \rightarrow \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \mathcal{S}$ such that \[u \mapsto u \hat\otimes u,~~~~v \mapsto u \hat\otimes v + v \hat\otimes u,\] where $u:=e^{-x^2}$, $v=xe^{-x^2}$.
<!-- end prop-16 -->
<!-- cor-8: body_md -->
\label{cor: s cocommutative coalgebra}
    The $*$-homomorphisms $\eta$ and $\triangle$ equip $\mathcal{S}$ with a cocommutative coalgebra structure; in the sense that the following diagrams commute
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathcal{S}} && {\mathcal{S} \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{S}} &&& {\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes \mathcal{S}} &&& {\mathcal{S}} & \\
	&&&& {\mathcal{S}} &&& {\mathcal{S}} && {\mathcal{S}} \\
	{\mathcal{S} \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{S}} && {\mathcal{S} \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{S} \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{S}} &&& {\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \mathcal{S}} &&& {\mathcal{S} \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{S}}
	\arrow["\Delta", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\Delta"', from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{1 \hat{\otimes} \Delta}", from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{flip}}", from=1-6, to=3-6]
	\arrow["{=}"', from=1-9, to=2-8]
	\arrow["{=}", from=1-9, to=2-10]
	\arrow["\Delta", from=1-9, to=3-9]
	\arrow["\Delta", from=2-5, to=1-6]
	\arrow["\Delta"', from=2-5, to=3-6]
	\arrow["{\Delta \hat{\otimes} 1}"', from=3-1, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{\eta \hat{\otimes} 1}", from=3-9, to=2-8]
	\arrow["{1 \hat{\otimes} \eta}"', from=3-9, to=2-10]
\end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end cor-8 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
This is immediate by considering the elements $u$ and $v$ in $\mathcal{S}$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
$\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}$ has a presentably symmetric monoidal structure for the graded tensor products $\hat{\otimes}_?$ for every choice of $(?,!)$ except $(?,!)=(\min,\operatorname{ex})$, and the canonical functor $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}$ has a symmetric monoidal refinement too.
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
We just discuss the separable analogue of the statement; the generalization to the large categories is a routine argument in light of the results of Section 3.7.
    
    One checks directly that each of the steps in the localizations 
    \[
\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}
\xrightarrow{L_h}
\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}
\xrightarrow{L_{\mathcal K_{G_2}}}
\mathrm S_{\mathcal K_{G_2}}\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_h^{\mathrm{sep}}
\xrightarrow{L_{!,\oplus}}
\mathrm S_{\mathcal K_{G_2}}\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h,!,\oplus_\omega}^{\mathrm{sep}}
\xrightarrow{L_{\operatorname{Bott}}}
\mathrm{KK}_{!,\infty}^{G_2,\mathrm{sep}}.
\]
    has a symmetric monoidal refinement for the graded tensor products, since under the restrictions imposed on $(?,!)$, it is clear that at each step $A \hat\otimes_!-$ preserves the class of morphisms that are inverted at that step (to see this for the excision step, we use that the underlying Banach spaces of the graded and ungraded tensor products coincide, see \cite[Lemma E.2.18]{WY}). The rest of the details are exactly as in the ungraded case.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- notn-5: body_md -->
Henceforth whenever we mention symmetric monoidal structures on equivariant $KK_{!,\infty}$ categories, we consider all choices of $(?,!)$ except $(?,!)=(\min,\operatorname{ex})$. We also stop decorating the tensor product every time; the decoration is implicitly assumed to be there abiding by the exception mentioned in the previous sentence.
<!-- end notn-5 -->
<!-- defi-17: body_md -->
\label{defi: KK-graded}
    The graded bivariant $KK^G_!$-category, denoted $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$, is the full subcategory spanned by cofree comodules in $\mathbf{Comod}_{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}}(\mathcal{S})$. Note that $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ becomes a symmetric monoidal category with respect to the balanced tensor product of comodules (\cite[Section 4.4]{HA}). 
    
    Denote by $\widehat{\mathrm{kk}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ the composition of the symmetric monoidal functors
    \[
    \widehat{\mathrm{kk}}^{G}_{!,\infty}: \mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{kk}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}} \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty} \xrightarrow{\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes -} \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}\
    \]
<!-- end defi-17 -->
<!-- rem-15: body_md -->
\label{lem: KKANA cat}
    The following remarks about \Cref{defi: KK-graded} are in order.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Explicitly written out, the relative tensor product of $\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A$ and $\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes B$ is $\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A \hat\otimes B$, with the codiagonal map $\mathcal{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \mathcal{S}$ being used to cancel out one action of $\mathcal{S}$. This also roughly shows why $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty} \xrightarrow{\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes -} \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ is symmetric monoidal.
        \item It is not clear if the category $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ is stable, since cofree comodules need not be closed under the formation of finite limits or colimits. Nevertheless, it is enriched over Spectra being the full subcategory of a stable $\infty$-category, as follows from the next point.
        \item At first glance, a natural solution to the above problem could seem to simply work with the category of all $\mathcal{S}$-comodules. But then, there is no reason for this category to be symmetric monoidal, since one does not have appropriate commutation of the tensor product with cosimplicial limits in general (necessary for the dual of \cite[Theorem 4.5.2.1]{HA} to be applicable). Note that the monoidality assertions in \cite[Definition 2.45]{BUNKELUDEWIG} are incorrect.
        \item In applications, it is more important to have symmetric monoidality of the graded bivariant $K$-categories than having presentability. Therefore we choose the definition above.
        \item \emph{Denote by $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}$ the homotopy category of $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$}. From the forgetful-cofree adjunction, we immediately get the hom groups in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}$ are given by
    \[
        {\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}}(A,B) \cong {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,0}}(\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A,B).
    \]
    The composite of $\varphi \in \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}(A,B)\cong\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,0}(\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A,B)$ and $\psi \in \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}(B,C)\cong\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,0}(\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes B,C)$ is given by the composite in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,0}$
    \[
    \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A\xrightarrow{\Delta \hat\otimes 1_A} \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A \xrightarrow{1_\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \varphi} \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes B \xrightarrow{\psi} C.
    \]
    The functor \[\widehat{\mathrm{kk}}^{G}_{!,0}:\mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \rightarrow \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}\] is identity on objects and precomposes with $\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A\xrightarrow{{\operatorname{ev}_0}_*} A$ on morphisms emanating out of $A$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end rem-15 -->
<!-- prop-17: body_md -->
\label{thm: kkgraeq vs kkctwoeq}
    If $A,B \in \mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$ are equivalent in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$, then $\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A$ and $\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes B$ are equivalent in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}$.
<!-- end prop-17 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
By \Cref{defi: KK-graded}, $A$ and $B$ are equivalent in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ means that we have an equivalence \[\mathrm{kk}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(\mathcal{S}) \hat\otimes \mathrm{kk}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(A)\simeq \mathrm{kk}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(\mathcal{S}) \hat\otimes \mathrm{kk}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(B)\] of cofree comodules. Invoking the functoriality of the forgetful functor $\mathbf{Comod}_{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}}(\mathcal{S}) \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}$ now finishes the argument.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{prop: equivalence KKgra and KKsp}
    For any \(\hat B\in\mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}\), we have a natural equivalence of spaces
\[
\mathbb{\hat K}^{G}(\hat B)
\simeq
\Omega^{\infty}\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}(\mathbb C,\hat B).
\]
Moreover,
\(
\hat K_0^G(-),\;
\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}(\mathbb C,-):
\mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Ab}
\)
are equivalent as lax monoidal functors.
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
This is an immediate consequence of \Cref{defi: KK-graded}, \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}, and \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}.4. The lax monoidality assertion follows  upon observing that the lax monoidality of $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(\mathcal{S},-)$ stems from the codiagonal map $\mathcal{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \mathcal{S}
    $ too, as mentioned in \Cref{lem: KKANA cat}.1.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
\label{thm: higson email to johannes}
    In the commutative square 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\[
\small
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}} &&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}} \\
	{\mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}} && {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}} & {\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}}
	\arrow["{\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{!,\infty}}", from=1-1, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(-)}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(-)}"{description}, from=1-4, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(-)}", from=1-4, to=2-4]
	\arrow["{\mathrm{kk}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}}"', from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes -}"', from=2-3, to=2-4]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
the right functor is fully faithful.
<!-- end thm-9 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
We have to show that the composite
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn: triv gra is ungra}
        \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}(A,B) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(-)} \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(A),\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(B)) \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_0^*} \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}(\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(A),\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(B))
    \end{equation}
    is an equivalence. To that end, we accommodate \Cref{eqn: triv gra is ungra} into the commutative diagram (note that the left part of the diagram commutes can be seen by explicitly calculating the fate of a $G$-equivariant homomorphism from $A$ to $B$ using the definition of the unit of the restriction-coinduction adjunction as described in \Cref{defi: change of groups}. The formulae of loc.\! cit.\! also work in the non-separable case)
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[
	column sep=1.2em,
	row sep=2.2em,
	scale=0.78,
	transform shape
]
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}(A,B)}
	&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}\!\left(\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(A),\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(B)\right)}
	&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}\!\left(
		\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(A),
		\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(B)
	\right)}
	\\
	{}
	&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}\!\left(
		\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(A)\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1},
		\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(B)\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}
	\right)}
	&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}\!\left(
		\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(A)\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1},
		\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(B)\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}
	\right)}
	\\
	{}
	&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}\!\left(
		\mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G(A\otimes Cl^{0,1}),B
	\right)}
	&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}\!\left(
		\mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G(\mathcal{S}\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})\otimes A,B
	\right)}
	\arrow["{\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(-)}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[
		"{(Cl^{0,1}_u\xrightarrow{\pi_1}\mathbb C)^*}"'{pos=0.4},
		bend right=24,
		from=1-1,
		to=3-2
	]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev}_0^*}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{-\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}}"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{-\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}}"', from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev}_0^*}", from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[
		"{\mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G\dashv\mathsf{coind}^{G_2}_G}"',
		from=2-2,
		to=3-2
	]
	\arrow[
		"{\mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G\dashv\mathsf{coind}^{G_2}_G}"',
		from=2-3,
		to=3-3
	]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev}_0^*}", from=3-2, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Note that we implicitly have used that $A$ and $B$ have the trivial grading so as to replace some graded tensor products with the ungraded ones.
In light of the above diagram, our thesis would follow once we have shown that the composite
\[
(\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u \xrightarrow{{\operatorname{ev}_0}_*} Cl^{0,1}_u \xrightarrow{\pi_1} \mathbb C
\]
is an equivalence in $\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{!,\infty}$. But this readily follows from \Cref{cor: s fib seqn}.3.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- defi-18: body_md -->
Let $V$ be a pseudo Euclidean vector space. Let $\iota: V \rightarrow Cl(V)$ denote the canonical inclusion of $V$ into $Cl(V)$. Then the functional calculus of $\iota$ yields a graded homomorphism
    \[
    b_V:\mathcal{S} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}(V),
    \]
    which we call the Bott map. It naturally determines a point in the spectral $K$-theory space
$
\mathbb{\hat K}\bigl(\mathcal C(V)\bigr),
$
and hence also a point in
$
\Omega^\infty \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty}
\bigl(\mathbb C,\mathcal C(V)\bigr).
$ In light of \Cref{prop: equivalence KKgra and KKsp},  we denote either of them by $b_V$.
<!-- end defi-18 -->
<!-- rem-16: body_md -->
\label{rem: Bott facts}
    \cite[Section 9]{D} contains a detailed proof that
$\pi_0\hat{\mathbb K}\bigl(\mathcal{C}(V)\bigr) \cong \mathbb Z$,
and that $b_V$ is a generator of this group. Consequently, $b_V$ is also a generator of
$\pi_0\operatorname{map}_{\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty}}\bigl(\mathbb C,\mathcal{C}(V)\bigr) \cong \mathbb Z$.
Furthermore, the proof of \Cref{prop: omnibus graded k-theory}.4 shows that
\[b_V \times b_{\overline V}
\in
\pi_0\hat{\mathbb K}\bigl(
\mathcal{C}(V)\hat\otimes\mathcal{C}(\overline V)
\bigr)
\cong \pi_0\hat{\mathbb{K}}(\mathcal{C}(V \oplus \overline{V})) \cong \mathbb Z\]
is a generator of the group.
<!-- end rem-16 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem: product of bott elements iso}
    For any pseudo-Euclidean vector space $V$, the morphism
\[
b_V \times b_{\overline V}
\in
\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}\bigl(\mathbb C,\mathcal{C}(V)\hat\otimes\mathcal{C}(\overline V)\bigr)
\]
is an isomorphism in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}$.
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
\Cref{rem: Bott facts} shows that $b_V \times b_{\overline{V}}$ is a unit in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}(\mathbb C, \mathcal{C}(V) \hat\otimes \mathcal{C}(\overline{V}))$. On the other hand, the Toeplitz extension theory shows that there is a $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}$-equivalence between $\mathbb C$ and $\mathcal{C}(V) \hat\otimes \mathcal{C}(\overline{V})$, given by the image of the boundary map of the Toeplitz extension under the canonical functor $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,0} \rightarrow \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}$. This also has to be a unit in $\mathbb Z$ because of the following general fact: in any additive $1$-category $\mathcal{D}$, if there are isomorphic objects $x$ and $y$ such that $\operatorname{hom}_{\mathcal{D}}(x,y) \cong \mathbb Z$ as abelian groups, then the isomorphism necessarily corresponds to $\pm 1$.\footnote{a proof of this fact can be deduced from the elementary algebra fact that any commutative unital ring structure on the abelian group $\mathbb Z$ must be isomorphic to the standard ring structure on $\mathbb Z$ (\cite[Exercise 2.16]{ALUFFI}).} To prove our thesis, we simply use that if $f$ is an isomorphism in an additive category, then so is $-f$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- thm-10: body_md -->
\label{thm: dirac-dual Dirac abstract}
For any pseudo Euclidean vector space $V$, the Bott element $b_V$ is an equivalence in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}$.
<!-- end thm-10 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
\label{lem: interchange law}
    Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a monoidal $(\infty)$-category, and let
$A,B,C,A',B',C'$ be objects of $\mathcal{C}$. For composable morphisms
\[
A \xrightarrow{f} B \xrightarrow{g} C,
\qquad
A' \xrightarrow{h} B' \xrightarrow{k} C',
\]
the functoriality of the tensor product
$
\otimes : \mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow\mathcal{C}
$
gives a canonical homotopy
\[
(g\circ f)\otimes(k\circ h)
\simeq
(g\otimes k)\circ(f\otimes h)
\]
in the mapping space
$
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal{C}}
(A\otimes A',\,C\otimes C').
$
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- lem-10: body_md -->
\label{lem: bott induces iso in KKANA}
    For any $X \in \widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$, the following diagram of abelian groups commutes 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: diagram KKGRA}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}(\mathcal{C}(V),X)}
	&&
	{\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}(\mathbb C,X)}
	\\
	{\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}\bigl(
		\mathcal{C}(V)\hat\otimes\mathcal{C}(\overline V),
		X\hat\otimes\mathcal{C}(\overline V)
	\bigr)}
	\\
	{\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}\bigl(
		\mathbb C,
		X\hat\otimes\mathcal{C}(\overline V)
	\bigr)}
	&&
	{\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}(\mathbb C,X)}
	\arrow["{b_V^*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{-\hat\otimes\mathcal{C}(\overline V)}", from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{=}", no head, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{(b_V\times b_{\overline V})^*}", from=2-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{-\times b_{\overline V}}"', from=3-3, to=3-1]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
Furthermore, all the arrows in the above diagram are isomorphisms.
<!-- end lem-10 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
That all the morphisms in the diagram are additive is clear. That it also commutes is an application of \Cref{lem: interchange law}. In the notation of loc.\! cit.\! we take
    \[
    \mathcal{C}:=\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}, A=A'=\mathbb C, B=\mathcal{C}(V), B'=C'=\mathcal{C}(\overline{V}), C=X.
    \]
    As for the morphisms, we can take any $g \in \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}(\mathcal{C}(V),X)$, and
    \[
    f=b_V, h=b_{\overline{V}}, k=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}(\overline{V})}.
    \]
