    Since \Cref{eqn: diagram KKGRA} commutes, it suffices to show that the two left vertical arrows and the bottom horizontal arrows are isomorphisms. That \[- \hat\otimes \mathcal{C}(\overline{V}): \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}(\mathcal{C}(V),X) \rightarrow \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}(\mathcal{C}(V) \hat\otimes \mathcal{C}(\overline{V}), X \hat\otimes \mathcal{C}(\overline{V}))\] is an isomorphism follows because tensoring with $\mathcal{C}(\overline{V})$ yields an isomorphism in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,0}$ (with the inverse being tensoring with $\mathcal{C}(V)$), and because the cofree comodule functor $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,\infty} \xrightarrow{\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes -} \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty}$ is symmetric monoidal. That $b_V \times b_{\overline{V}}$ is an isomorphism follows from \Cref{lem: product of bott elements iso}, and the bottom horizontal arrow being an isomorphism is the content of \cite[Theorem 9.13]{D}.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- rem-17: body_md -->
We mention that the proof of \cite[Theorem 9.13]{D} uses non-trivial functional analysis and features of classical graded $K$-theory (such as graded asymptotic morphisms between graded $C^*$-algebras induce morphisms between the graded $K$-groups). However,  the ``$K$-theoretic" result is enough for the proof of \Cref{lem: bott induces iso in KKANA}, and we do not need to know that there is any relation between the $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,0}$ categories and asymptotic morphisms. And indeed, when $!=\operatorname{se}$, a general asymptotic morphism would not induce a morphism in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{\mathrm{se},0}$.
<!-- end rem-17 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
This readily follows from the Yoneda lemma and \Cref{lem: bott induces iso in KKANA}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- cor-9: body_md -->
\label{cor: loops is clifford one zero}
    In $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$, we have an equivalence $C_0(V) \simeq Cl(\overline{V})$. In particular, the functor
    \[
    - \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0}:\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty} \rightarrow \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}
    \]
    is equivalent to the loops functor on $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$.
<!-- end cor-9 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
We begin by first observing that \Cref{thm: dirac-dual Dirac abstract} also shows that the Bott element is an equivalence in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$. This is because $\mathbb{C}$ and $\mathcal{C}(V)$ have the trivial $G$-action, and we have an obvious ``equipping with the trivial $G$-action" functor $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty} \rightarrow \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$.\footnote{More formally, we could have developed a graded variant of the change of group functors, and deduced this from the functoriality of the restriction functor. But because we would not have the occassion to use it anywhere else, we omit the details.}
    
    It suffices to show that $C_0(V)$ and ${Cl}(\overline{V})$ are isomorphic in $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,0}$. But this follows from the implications
    \[
    \mathbb C \cong \mathcal{C}(V) \implies Cl(\overline{V}) \cong C_0(V) \hat\otimes Cl(V) \hat\otimes Cl(\overline{V}) \implies Cl(\overline{V}) \cong C_0(V),
    \]
    where we used that tensoring with $Cl(\overline{V})$ is already an isomorphism in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,0}$, and because $\mathbb C \rightarrow Cl(V \oplus \overline{V})$ is a $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,0}$-equivalence.
    
    The last assertion follows from the observation that the canonical functor $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty} \rightarrow \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}$ is left-exact, and loops in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}$ is modeled by $C_0(\mathbb R^{0,1})$.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- prop-18: body_md -->
\label{prop: graded kk not dk loc}
    The full subcategory of $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty}$ spanned by separable, graded $C^*$-algebras (denoted $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty}^{\operatorname{sep}}$) is not the Dwyer-Kan localization of the category of separable, graded $C^*$-algebras at any class of morphisms.
<!-- end prop-18 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Since the grading on a graded $C^*$-algebra induces a $C_2$-action on the graded $K$-groups, we have a commutative diagram of functors
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	&& {C_2\!\operatorname{-Ab}} \\
	{\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}} && {\operatorname{Ab}} \\
	\\
	{\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{\mathrm{sep}}_{!,\infty}}
	\arrow["{\operatorname{forget}}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\hat{K}_0(-)}", from=2-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\hat{K}_0(-)}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\widehat{\mathrm{kk}}^{\mathrm{sep}}_{!,\infty}}"', from=2-1, to=4-1]
	\arrow["{\pi_0\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{\mathrm{sep}}_{!,\infty}(\mathbb C,-)}"', from=4-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Note that the bottom triangle commutes from \Cref{prop: equivalence KKgra and KKsp}. But since the forgetful functor $C_2\!\operatorname{-Ab} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}$ reflects isomorphisms, had $\widehat{KK}_{!,\infty}^{\operatorname{sep}}$ been a Dwyer-Kan localization, we would obtain a lift in the above diagram $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty}^{\operatorname{sep}} \rightarrow C_2\!\operatorname{-Ab}$, and thereby conclude that the $\hat{K}_0$-groups of two $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{!,\infty}^{\operatorname{sep}}$-equivalent $C^*$-algebras are in fact isomorphic as $C_2$-abelian groups. In light of \Cref{thm: dirac-dual Dirac abstract}, this a contradiction, since $\hat{K}_0(\mathbb C) \cong \mathbb Z$ with the trivial $C_2$-action, whereas $\hat{K}_0(C_0(\mathbb R,Cl^{0,1})) \cong \mathbb Z$ with the action $n \mapsto -n$, as shown in \Cref{prop: omnibus graded k-theory}.4.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- rem-18: body_md -->
Note that there is an obvious equivariant version of \Cref{prop: graded kk not dk loc} too.
<!-- end rem-18 -->
<!-- rem-19: body_md -->
\label{rem: obvious}
        We will be using the following elementary observations in this section even without mentioning.
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item The datum of a $G \times H$-action on a $C^*$-algebra $A$ is same as the datum of a $G$-action and a $H$-action on $A$ \emph{which commute}. Under this identification, it makes sense to talk about the $G$- and $H$-actions on a $(G\times H)$-$C^*$-algebra. Similar comment also applies to equivariant projective modules. For $G_2$-equivariant projective modules, we will be omitting the $G$-action from the notation, and just keep track of the $C_2$-action. For example, \emph{when we write $(A,\alpha) \in \mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$, we mean the $C_2$-action is given by $\alpha$.}
            \item Suppose $A,B,C \in \mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$ have trivial $G$-action, and fit in a fiber sequence in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,\infty}$. Then, since $\operatorname{res}^{C_2}_{G_2}$ is left-exact, they also fit in a fiber sequence in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{!,\infty}$.
            \item  With \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen} and \Cref{prop: equivalence KKgra and KKsp} at our disposal, we will henceforth be (abusing notation and) denoting by $\mathbb{K}^G$ (resp. $\hat{\mathbb{K}}^G$) the $G$-equivariant (resp. graded $G$-equivariant) $K$-theory \emph{spectra}, given by $KK_{!,\infty}^{G}(\mathbb C,-)$ (resp. $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}^{G}_{!,\infty}(\mathbb C,-) \simeq KK_{!,\infty}^{G_2}(\mathcal{S},-)$). As before, we will be denoting their homotopy groups by $K_*^G(-)$ (resp. $\hat{K}_*^G(-)$).
            \item \emph{In the remainder of this section, we fix a compact group $G$.}  For concreteness, we work with $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$ in this section. The same calculations can also be done with $KK_{\operatorname{se},\infty}^{G_2}$.
        \end{enumerate}
<!-- end rem-19 -->
<!-- prop-19: body_md -->
\label{lem: fib seqn}
    We have a natural fiber sequence of spectra \begin{equation}\label{eqn: first fib seqn}
         \mathbb{K}^G(A_u) \rightarrow \mathbb{K}^{G_2}(A) \rightarrow \hat{\mathbb{K}}^G(A)
    \end{equation}
    for every $A \in \mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$.
<!-- end prop-19 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Upon applying the exact functor
\[
\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(-,A): \mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg} \longrightarrow \operatorname{Sp}
\]
to the fiber sequence of \Cref{cor: s fib seqn}.2, we are done once we justify the maps $(1)$, $(2)$, and $(3)$ in the following diagram:
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{0,1},A)}
	&&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)}
	&&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathcal{S},A)}
	\\
	{\mathbb K^G(A_u)}
	&&
	{\mathbb K^{G_2}(A)}
	&&
	{\hat{\mathbb K}^{G}(A)}
	\arrow["{\iota^*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\simeq\,(1)}"', tail reversed, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev}_0^*}", from=1-3, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\simeq\,(2)}"', tail reversed, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\simeq\,(3)}"', tail reversed, from=1-5, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The map labeled $(1)$ arises from the induction-restriction adjunction (\Cref{thm: change of group general}), since we can identify
$
\mathsf{ind}^{G_2}_G \mathbb{C}$ with $Cl^{0,1}$.
The second and third equivalence follow from \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- rem-20: body_md -->
We claim that there is a fiber sequence 
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn: another formulation}
        \mathbb{K}^G(A_u) \xrightarrow{(A\rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_* } \mathbb{K}^G((A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u) \rightarrow \hat{\mathbb{K}}^G(A)
    \end{equation}
    which is equivalent to the fiber sequence in \Cref{eqn: first fib seqn}. Indeed, this will follow from the following commutative diagram
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: abs formulation fib seqn}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\begin{tikzcd}
	&&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)} \\
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{0,1},A)} &&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{0,1},A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})} \\
	\\
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A_u)} &&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,(A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u)}
	\arrow["{-\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}}", from=1-4, to=2-4]
	\arrow["{\iota^*}", from=2-1, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{(A\rightarrow A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_*}"', from=2-1, to=2-4]
	\arrow["{\mathsf{ind}^{G_2}_G \dashv \mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G}"', from=2-1, to=4-1]
	\arrow["{\mathsf{ind}^{G_2}_G \dashv \mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G}", from=2-4, to=4-4]
	\arrow["{(A\rightarrow A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_*}"', from=4-1, to=4-4]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
Note that the top triangle commutes because the diagram below commutes in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$, where $f: Cl^{0,1} \rightarrow A$ is any morphism in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$. The left triangle below \emph{does not} commute at the level of algebras, but only up to homotopy.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: Morita move}
    \begin{tikzcd}
	&& {Cl^{0,1}} && A \\
	{Cl^{0,1}} && {Cl^{0,2}} && {A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}}
	\arrow["f", from=1-3, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{=}"', no head, from=1-3, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{1_{Cl^{0,1}} \hat\otimes \iota}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{1_A \hat\otimes \iota}", from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow["{\iota \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}}"', from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{f \hat\otimes 1_{Cl^{0,1}}}"', from=2-3, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
<!-- end rem-20 -->
<!-- rem-21: body_md -->
\label{rem: abs style seqn}
    We claim there is a fiber sequence
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn: fib seq ABS style}
         \mathbb{K}^{G_2}(A \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0}) \xrightarrow{(A \rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0})^*} \mathbb{K}^{G_2}(A) \rightarrow \hat{\mathbb{K}}^G(A)
    \end{equation}
   which is equivalent to the fiber sequence in \Cref{eqn: first fib seqn}. The map labeled $A \rightarrow (A \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0})^*$ should be taken with a pinch of salt as $\mathbb{K}^{G_2}(-)$ is naturally covariantly functorial; what we mean is the map obtained from the zig-zag \[A\hat\otimes Cl^{1,0} \rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{1,1} \xleftarrow{\simeq} A.\] When $A$ is unital, it can be shown (\cite[Section 4.5.2]{AS}) that on $\pi_0$, this has the same effect as precomposing the structure map of a $G_2$-equivariant $A \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0}$ projective module with the homomorphism $A \rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0}$. The equivalence of the fiber sequences in \Cref{eqn: first fib seqn} and \Cref{eqn: fib seq ABS style} can be shown by a similar treatment as in the last remark.

    This formulation of the fiber sequence is directly related to the classical Atiyah-Bott-Shapiro description of $K$-groups of a point, see \Cref{rem: abs} for more details.
<!-- end rem-21 -->
<!-- prop-20: body_md -->
When $A$ is inner graded, the fiber sequence in \Cref{eqn: first fib seqn} (and hence also the ones in \Cref{eqn: another formulation} and \Cref{eqn: fib seq ABS style}) splits.
<!-- end prop-20 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
In light of \Cref{eqn: another formulation}, we have to show that the map of spectra
    \[
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A_u)
\xrightarrow{(A\to A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_*}
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}\bigl(\mathbb C,(A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u\bigr).
\]
    has a retraction when $A$ is inner graded. In this case, since $A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1} \cong A \otimes Cl^{0,1}$ in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$, we can extend the aforementioned map to
   \[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A_u)
&\xrightarrow{(A\to A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_*}
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}\bigl(\mathbb C,(A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u\bigr)
\\
&\xrightarrow{\simeq}
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}\bigl(\mathbb C,(A\otimes Cl^{0,1})_u\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\simeq}
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A_u\oplus A_u)
\\
&\xrightarrow{\simeq}
\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A_u)\oplus \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A_u).
\end{aligned}
\]
    It can be directly checked that this composite is the diagonal map of $KK_{\operatorname{ex},\infty}^{G}(\mathbb C,A_u)$. Since the diagonal map of any spectrum has two canonical retractions, we are done.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- rem-22: body_md -->
At this stage, the reader may want to see an example where the fiber sequence in \Cref{eqn: first fib seqn} does not split. This is intimately related to a folklore question (\Cref{que: que}), and we discuss it in \Cref{rem: abs}.
<!-- end rem-22 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\label{lemlem}
    Let $(A,\alpha)$ be a unital algebra in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$. We have a natural group homomorphism
    \[
    F_A:K_0^{G_2}(A) \rightarrow {K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A)
    \]
   given by taking a finitely generated $G_2$-equivariant projective $A$-module $M$ to the Fredholm cycle $(M,0) \in K_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A)$.
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
The assertion is clear, modulo the verification that every finitely generated $G_2$-equivariant projective $A$-module is canonically a graded $G$-equivariant Hilbert $A$-module. This follows by an easy case by case analysis with signs in light of \cite[Proposition 11.2.3]{BLAK}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- cor-10: body_md -->
Following the notation of \Cref{lemlem}, the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\pi_0\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)}
	&&
	{\pi_0\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathcal{S},A)}
	\\
	{K_0^{G_2}(A)}
	&&
	{\hat{K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A)}
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev}_0^*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\cong", from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{F_A}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes.
<!-- end cor-10 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Given a $G_2$-equivariant projective $A$-module $M$, we study the fate of $[M] \in K_0^{G_2}(A)$ along the up-right-down itinerary. 

    The classifying map of $M$ is a $G_2$-equivariant $*$-homomorphism 
    \[
    \varphi: \mathbb C \rightarrow \mathcal{K}_A(V \otimes A),
    \]
    where $V$ is a finite dimensional $G_2$-vector space. $\varphi$ is the image of $[M]$  in $\pi_0(KK_{\operatorname{ex},\infty}^{G_2}(\mathbb{C},A))$ under the left vertical map, as can be seen by unraveling the maps in \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen} and the equivariant Kasparov stabilization theorem. Also note that $\mathcal{K}_A(V \otimes A)= \mathcal{B}_A(V \otimes A)$ since $\mathcal{K}_A(V \otimes A)$ is unital, see \cite[Theorem 15.4.2]{WG}. It remains to determine the image of $\operatorname{\varphi \circ ev_0}$ under the right vertical map. From \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}.5, one gets that this image is the Fredholm cycle (we are also using the notation of the proof of \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}.5) \[(\overline{\varphi \circ \operatorname{ev}_0(\mathcal{S})(V \otimes A)},\Tilde{\varphi}(x))=(M,0)\]
    Indeed, this follows from the commutative diagram 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathcal{S}} & {\mathcal{K}_A(\overline{\varphi \circ \operatorname{ev}_0(\mathcal{S})(V \otimes A)})} & {\mathcal{K}_A(V \otimes A)} \\
	{C[-1,1]} & {\mathbb{C}}
	\arrow["{(\varphi \circ \operatorname{ev}_0)^{\operatorname{nd}}}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev}_0}"{pos=0.8}, from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\iota", from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\exists !}"{pos=0.1}, dashed, from=2-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev}_0}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\varphi^{\operatorname{nd}}}"', from=2-2, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\varphi"', from=2-2, to=1-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
The dotted extension of $(\varphi \circ \operatorname{ev}_0)^{\operatorname{nd}}$ is unique. However, $\varphi^{\operatorname{nd}}\circ \operatorname{ev}_0$ is yet another extension, whence they must agree. Our thesis is deduced readily from the latter.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- notn-6: body_md -->
Let $(A,\alpha) \in \mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$. Denote by $A_\alpha$ the $G$-equivariant $A_u$-module $\underline{A}$ (the underlying abelian group of $A$) with the $A_u$-action given by $\underline{a}.b:=\underline{a\alpha(b)}$ and the $G$-action given by $g.\underline{a}:=\underline{ga}$. Note that $A_\alpha$ is a $A_u$-$A_u$ bimodule in a canonical way.
<!-- end notn-6 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{lem: GA definition}
    Let $(A,\alpha)$ be a unital algebra in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$. We have a natural group homomorphism
    \[
    G_A:K_0^G(A_u) \rightarrow K_0^{G_2}(A)
    \]
given by taking a finitely generated $G$-equivariant projective $A_u$-module $M$ to the $G_2$-equivariant finitely generated projective $A$-module $M \oplus M_\alpha$, where $M_{\alpha}:=M \otimes_{A_u} A_{\alpha}$\footnote{explicitly, $M_\alpha$ is the abelian group $\underline{M}$ with the $A_u$-action given by $\underline{m}.a:=\underline{m\alpha(a)}$. $M$ and $M_{\alpha}$ are not isomorphic as  $A_u$-modules in general.} and the $C_2$-action on $M \oplus M_{\tau}$ is flip, i.e. given by $(m,\underline{n}) \mapsto (n,\underline{m})$.
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Obvious.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- cor-11: body_md -->
\label{cor: map induced by C in CL01}
    Following the notation of \Cref{lem: GA definition}, the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\pi_0\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{0,1},A)}
	&&
	{\pi_0\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)}
	\\
	{K_0^G(A_u)}
	&&
	{K_0^{G_2}(A)}
	\arrow["{\iota^*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\cong", from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{G_A}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes.
<!-- end cor-11 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
This follows by chasing through the maps in the diagram. Given a $G$-equivariant finitely generated projective $A_u$-module $M$, the classifying map of $[M] \in K_0(A_u)$ is a $G$-equivariant $*$-homomorphism
    \[
    p:\mathbb{C} \rightarrow \mathcal{K}_{A_u}(V \otimes A_u)
    \]
    where $V$ is some finite dimensional $G$-vector space. We therefore obtain
    \[
    \operatorname{ind}^{G_2}_G \mathbb C \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ind}^{G_2}_Gp} \operatorname{ind}^{G_2}_G(\mathcal{K}_{A_u}(V \otimes A_u)) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{K}_A(V \otimes A_u \oplus V \otimes A_u, \operatorname{twisted~flip}),
    \]
    where for the last inclusion we used elementary properties of induction for group representations on vector spaces and $C^*$-algebras (see \cite[Lemma 4.10]{BEL}), as well as the description of the co-unit of the induction-restriction adjunction. Precomposing with the inclusion $\mathbb C \rightarrow \operatorname{ind}^{G_2}_G \mathbb C$, we conclude that the up-right-down itinerary maps $p$ to the homomorphism
    \[
    \tilde{p}: \mathbb C \rightarrow \mathcal{K}_A(V \otimes A_u \oplus V \otimes A_u, \operatorname{twisted~flip}), ~~~~\tilde{p}(1)=(p(1) \oplus\alpha_*p(1)).
    \]
    It remains to check that the $G_2$-equivariant $A$-modules $(p(1)(V \otimes A_u) \oplus \alpha_*p(1)(V \otimes A_u), \operatorname{twisted~flip})~$and $(M \oplus M_\alpha,\operatorname{flip})$ are isomorphic. We have $p(1)(V \otimes A_u) \cong M$ as $G$-equivariant $A_u$-modules by definition. To see that $\alpha_*p(1)(V \otimes A_u) \cong M_{\alpha}$ as $G$-equivariant $A_u$-modules, note that we have 
    \[
    \alpha_*p(1)(V \otimes A_u)=\{v \otimes \alpha a \mid v \otimes a \in p(1)(V \otimes A_u)\}.
    \]
    The map
    \begin{align*}
        \varphi: (p(1)(V \otimes A_u))_{\alpha} &\rightarrow \alpha_*p(1)(V \otimes A_u) \\
        \underline{v \otimes a} &\mapsto v\otimes \alpha(a)
    \end{align*}
 now readily produces an isomorphism between the $G$-equivariant $A_u$-modules $M_\alpha$ and $\alpha_*p(1)(V \otimes A_u)$. It is now also direct to check that juxtaposing the two isomorphisms yields a $G_2$-equivariant isomorphism between $(M \oplus M_\alpha,\operatorname{flip})$ and $(p(1)(V \otimes A_u) \oplus \alpha_*p(1)(V \otimes A_u), \operatorname{twisted~flip}).$
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- rem-23: body_md -->
\label{rem: abs}
    When $A=Cl^{n,0}$, Atiyah-Bott-Shapiro asserts that there are short exact sequences of abelian groups
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn: abs classical}
         0 \rightarrow K_0^{C_2}(Cl^{n+1,0}) \xrightarrow{(Cl^{n,0} \rightarrow Cl^{n+1,0})^*} K_0^{C_2}(Cl^{n,0}) \rightarrow \hat{K}_0(Cl^{n,0}) \rightarrow 0,
    \end{equation}
    where the first map is as described in \Cref{rem: abs style seqn}. Since $\hat{K}_0(Cl^{n,0}) \cong K_n(\mathbb C)$, one obtains a convenient (and perhaps miraculous!) description of higher $K$-groups of a point as certain \emph{Clifford module quotients}. This immediately makes one ask the following question.
    \begin{que}\label{que: que}
        Can the higher $K$-groups of any (graded), (Real) unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ be expressed in terms of Clifford module quotients a'la Atiyah-Bott-Shapiro? More precisely, does there exist a short exact sequence of abelian groups of the form
        \[
        0 \rightarrow K_0^{C_2}(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n+1,0}) \xrightarrow{(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n,0} \rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{n+1,0})^*} K_0^{C_2}(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n,0}) \rightarrow \hat{K}_n(A) \rightarrow 0~~~~~~~~~~?
        \]
    \end{que}
    We explain that the answer to this question is in the negative. To that end, we recall that to show exactness of \Cref{eqn: abs classical} at $\hat{K}_0(Cl^{n,0})$, one explicitly constructs a section of the map $K_0^{C_2}(Cl^{n,0}) \rightarrow \hat{K}_0(Cl^{n,0})$ using the notion of index of a Fredholm operator on a \emph{Hilbert space} with Clifford symmetries. The construction of this index map crucially needs the analytic fact that the kernel of a Fredholm operator on a Hilbert space is automatically finitely generated projective. Since the same is not true for a general Hilbert module over a $C^*$-algebra, the index of a Fredholm operator over an \emph{ungraded} unital $C^*$-algebra $B$ is typically defined using the notion of \emph{taming} (as described in detail in \cite[Section 8.2]{D}). Roughly speaking, taming works by adding a dummy finite dimensional free $B$-module to the game, and then  subtracting it later in the group $K_0(B)$. When $B$ is \emph{graded}, the taming construction can fail; for example when $B:=A \hat\otimes Cl^{n,0}$ the taming construction can be seen to not necessarily preserve the relevant Clifford symmetries. So in general, one cannot expect to construct the crucial index map witnessing a section of the map $K_0^{C_2}(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n,0}) \rightarrow \hat{K}_0(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n,0})$.
    
    And indeed, concrete counterexamples exist. Taking $A$ to be the complex $C^*$-algebra $C(S^1,\mathbb C)$ and $n=1$, we know that $\hat{K}_1(C(S^1,\mathbb C)) \cong K_1(C(S^1,\mathbb C)) \cong \mathbb Z$, but the relevant {Clifford module quotient} can be shown to be $0$. In context of the fiber sequence in \Cref{eqn: fib seq ABS style}, this failure can be explained to be due to the corresponding boundary map being injective. More elaborations on this can be found in \cite[Example 4.51]{AS}. See also \cite[Appendix A]{KOEN} for other examples and discussions.
<!-- end rem-23 -->
<!-- que-1: body_md -->
\label{que: que}
        Can the higher $K$-groups of any (graded), (Real) unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ be expressed in terms of Clifford module quotients a'la Atiyah-Bott-Shapiro? More precisely, does there exist a short exact sequence of abelian groups of the form
        \[
        0 \rightarrow K_0^{C_2}(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n+1,0}) \xrightarrow{(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n,0} \rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{n+1,0})^*} K_0^{C_2}(A \hat\otimes Cl^{n,0}) \rightarrow \hat{K}_n(A) \rightarrow 0~~~~~~~~~~?
        \]
<!-- end que-1 -->
<!-- prop-21: body_md -->
\label{prop: Cl10 fib seqn}
    We have a fiber sequence
    \[
    Cl^{1,0} \xrightarrow{j}\mathbb{C} \xrightarrow{p} \mathcal{S}
    \]
    in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$, where $j:Cl^{1,0} \rightarrow \mathbb C$ is obtained from the zig-zag
    $
    Cl^{1,0} \rightarrow Cl^{1,1} \leftarrow \mathbb C,
    $
    and $p \in \pi_0(\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,\mathcal{S}))$ is the image under the $\operatorname{res}^{C_2}_{G_2}$ homomorphism of a generator of $K_0^{C_2}(\mathcal{S})\cong \mathbb Z$ (\Cref{prop: K0C2S}).
<!-- end prop-21 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
We begin the proof by mentioning that the assertion of the proposition is indeed just: in any stable $\infty$-category $\mathcal{C}$, a fiber sequence $A \xrightarrow{f} B \xrightarrow{g} C$ naturally yields a equivalent fiber sequence $A \xrightarrow{f} B \xrightarrow{-g} C$. In light of \Cref{rem: obvious}.2, it suffices to demonstrate the existence of the fiber sequence in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$.
    
    We begin by applying the functor $- \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0}$ to \Cref{eq: s fib seqn}, thereby obtaining the fiber sequence
    \[
    \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes Cl^{1,0} \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_0{_*}} Cl^{1,0} \xrightarrow{\operatorname{\iota}_*} Cl^{1,1}.
    \]
    Now, \Cref{thm: kkgraeq vs kkctwoeq} and \Cref{cor: loops is clifford one zero} show that we have a fiber sequence 
    \[
    \Omega\mathcal{S} \rightarrow Cl^{1,0} \xrightarrow{\iota_*} Cl^{1,1}
    \]
    in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$. Taking cofibering in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$ and using the equivalence $\mathbb{C} \simeq Cl^{1,1}$ we obtain a fiber sequence
    \[
    Cl^{1,0} \xrightarrow{j} \mathbb{C} \rightarrow \mathcal{S}.
    \]
    To prove our thesis, it will suffice to show that the second morphism above is a generator of $K_0^{C_2}(\mathcal{S}) \cong \mathbb Z$. Consider the long exact sequence of $K_*^{C_2}(-)(=\pi_*\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,-))$ groups associated to this fiber sequence
    \[
    ... \rightarrow K_0^{C_2}(Cl^{1,0}) \xrightarrow{j_*} K_0^{C_2}(\mathbb C) \rightarrow K_0^{C_2}(\mathcal{S}) \xrightarrow{\partial} K_{-1}^{C_2}(Cl^{1,0}) \rightarrow ...
    \]
    By tensor invertibility of $Cl^{0,1}$ in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$ and the induction-restriction adjunction, we have \[
     K_{-1}^{C_2}(Cl^{1,0})  \cong K_{-1}(\mathbb{C}_u) \cong 0, 
    \]
    whence the map 
    \[
    K_0^{C_2}(\mathbb C) \rightarrow K_0^{C_2}(\mathcal{S}) 
    \]
    above is surjective. We now consider the square
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{K_0^{C_2}(\mathbb{C})} && {K_0^{C_2}(\mathcal{S})} \\
	{\mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}} && {\mathbb{Z}}
	\arrow[two heads, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\cong", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\dag", two heads, from=2-1, to=2-3],
\end{tikzcd}\]
where the vertical maps are isomorphisms as mentioned in \Cref{prop: KOC2} and \Cref{prop: K0C2S}, and the map $\dagger$ is so defined to make the diagram commute. Now, since the morphisms in the square are also $C_2$-equivariant and the $C_2$-abelian group $\mathbb Z \oplus \mathbb Z$ is generated by $(1,0)$, we conclude from the surjectivity of $\dag$ that it maps $(1,0)$ to $\pm1$.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- prop-22: body_md -->
\label{lem: dual fib seqn}
    We have a natural fiber sequence 
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn: dual fiber sequence}
            \hat{\mathbb{K}}^G(A) \xrightarrow{} \mathbb{K}^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{} \mathbb{K}^G((A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,2})_u)
    \end{equation}

    for every $A \in \mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$.
<!-- end prop-22 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
We apply the exact functor \[
\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(-,A):
\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Sp}.
\] to the fiber sequence in \Cref{prop: Cl10 fib seqn}. In light of the proof of \Cref{lem: fib seqn}, we only need to identify $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,0},A)$ with $\mathbb{K}^G((A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,2})_u)$. For that we use the route
    \[
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{$
\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,0},A)
\xrightarrow[\simeq]{-\hat\otimes Cl^{0,2}}
\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,2},A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,2})
\xrightarrow[\simeq]{(Cl^{0,1}\rightarrow Cl^{1,2})^*}
\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{0,1},A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,2})
\xrightarrow[\simeq]{\mathsf{ind}\dashv\mathsf{res}}
\mathbb{K}^G\bigl((A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,2})_u\bigr)
$}.
\]
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lem-13: body_md -->
\label{lem: another description of j star}
    The diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)}
	&&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,0},A)}
	\\
	{}
	&&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,1},A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})}
	\\
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)}
	&&
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})}
	\\
	{} & {}
	\arrow["{j^*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{=}", no head, from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1},\,\simeq}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{(\mathbb C\rightarrow Cl^{1,1})_*,\,\simeq}", from=2-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{(A\rightarrow A\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_*}", from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes.
<!-- end lem-13 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
We expand the diagram to
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)} &&&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,0},A)} \\
	{} & {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,1},A)} &&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,1},A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})} \\
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)} &&&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})} \\
	{} & {}
	\arrow["{j^*}", from=1-1, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{=}", no head, from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{\hat\otimes Cl^{0,1}}", from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow["{(\mathbb C \rightarrow Cl^{1,1})^*}"{description}, from=2-2, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{(Cl^{1,0} \rightarrow Cl^{1,1})^*}"{description}, from=2-2, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{(A \rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_*}"', from=2-2, to=2-5]
	\arrow["{(\mathbb C \rightarrow Cl^{1,1})^*}"{description}, from=2-2, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{(\mathbb C \rightarrow Cl^{1,1})^*}", from=2-5, to=3-5]
	\arrow["{(A \rightarrow A \hat\otimes Cl^{0,1})_*}", from=3-1, to=3-5]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
It suffices to show that each of the four shapes with one vertex $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,1},A)$ commutes. But all of them are clear (for the right-angled triangle shaped diagram, use an argument similar to the one for \Cref{eqn: Morita move}).
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lem-14: body_md -->
\label{lem: endo of K0C2}
    $\operatorname{ev}_0 \circ p = 1-x \in \mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C) \cong \frac{Z[x]}{x^2=1}$, with the isomorphism being as in \Cref{prop: KOC2}.1 (keeping in mind \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}\footnote{the two natural ring structures on the endomorphisms of the unit in any monoidal category coincide thanks to the Eckmann-Hilton argument. See also \cite[Lemma 5.1]{BUNLANPEN}.}).
<!-- end lem-14 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
From \Cref{prop: KOC2 CL01} and \Cref{prop: K0C2S}, we have a short exact sequence
    \[
    0\rightarrow K_0^{C_2}(\mathcal{S}) \xrightarrow{{\operatorname{ev}_0}_*} K_0^{C_2}(\mathbb C) \xrightarrow{\iota_*} K_0^{C_2}(Cl^{0,1})\rightarrow 0.
    \]
    The composition in the $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}$-category will be the image of $p$ under $\operatorname{ev_{0_*}}$. The rest follows from \Cref{prop: KOC2S to KOC2C commutes}.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- cor-12: body_md -->
\label{cor: ev0 circ p is mult by 2}
    The diagram                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} && {\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} \\
	\mathbb Z && \mathbb Z
	\arrow["{(\operatorname{ev}_0 \circ p)_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong", from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\cong", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{n \mapsto 2n}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes.
<!-- end cor-12 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
It suffices to show that the diagram commutes on $[\operatorname{ev}_0]$. The bottom-right itinerary maps it to $2 \in \mathbb Z$. To analyse its fate under the right-down itinerary, we bring \Cref{lem: endo of K0C2} into play, which shows that the upper horizontal arrow is product in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{!,\infty}$-product with $([\mathbb C^{\operatorname{triv}}]-[\mathbb C^{\operatorname{sign}}])$. 
   
    Postcomposition with $[\mathbb C]^{\operatorname{triv}}$ maps $[\operatorname{ev}_0]$ to itself, since $[\mathbb C^{\operatorname{triv}}]$ is the identity element of $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$. To prove our thesis, we have to show that postcomposition with $[\mathbb C^{\operatorname{sign}}]$ maps $[\operatorname{ev}_0]$ to $-[\operatorname{ev}_0]$. Unraveling the definition of postcomposition with $[\mathbb C^{\operatorname{sign}}]$, this follows directly from the proof of \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}.1.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- cor-13: body_md -->
Let $A$ be a unital algebra in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$. The composite
    \[
    K_0^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{0}^*} \hat{K}^G_0(A) \xrightarrow{p^*} K^{G_2}_0(A)
    \]
    maps a finitely generated $G_2$-equivariant projective $A$-module $M$ to $[M]-[M^{\operatorname{op}}] \in K_0^{G_2}(A)$, where $M^{\operatorname{op}}$ is $M$ as a $G$-equivariant $A_u$-module, with the $C_2$-action given as the negative of the $C_2$-action on $M$.
<!-- end cor-13 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Unraveling the definitions and from \Cref{lem: endo of K0C2}, we conclude that the composite is nothing but the composition with the image under $\operatorname{res}^{C_2}_{G_2}$ of $1-x \in \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C) \cong \frac{Z[x]}{x^2=1}$. Identifying $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$ with the classical $G_2$-equivariant $K$-theory of a point, it is clear that $1$ corresponds to the trivial representation, and $x$ corresponds to the sign representation of $G_2$ on $\mathbb C$.\footnote{more precisely, $G$ acts trivially on $\mathbb C$ in both cases, and $C_2$ acts either trivially or via the sign representation.} Since the internal and external products
    \[
    \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C) \times \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,A) \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,A)
    \]
    are the same (this is true in any monoidal category), our thesis follows since the external multiplication of $[M]$ with $x$ yields $[M^{\operatorname{op}}]$ (keeping in mind the lax monoidality assertion of \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}).
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lem-15: body_md -->
\label{lem: 1 plus x is the composition}
    $p \circ \operatorname{ev}_0=1+x \in \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}) \cong \frac{Z[x]}{x^2=1}$, with the isomorphism being as in \Cref{cor: EC2 SS ring}.
<!-- end lem-15 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
From the fiber sequence of \Cref{prop: Cl10 fib seqn}, 
    we obtain a long exact sequence of $\hat{K}_*(-)(=\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},-))$ groups
  \[
\cdots \longrightarrow
\hat K_0(Cl^{1,0})
\xrightarrow{j_*}
\hat K_0(\mathbb C)
\xrightarrow{p_*}
\hat K_0(\mathcal{S})
\xrightarrow{\partial}
\cdots
\]
    The composition $p \circ \operatorname{ev}_0$ will be the image of $[\operatorname{ev}_0]$ under $p_*$. Since $p_*$ is a $C_2$-equivariant map, there exists $k \in \mathbb Z$ rendering the diagram                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: commuting upto sign}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\hat K_0(\mathbb C)} && {\hat K_0(\mathcal{S})} \\
	\mathbb Z && {\mathbb Z \oplus \mathbb Z}
	\arrow["{p_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong"', no head, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{1 \mapsto (k,k)}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
commutative, where the left isomorphism is the standard one (mapping $[\operatorname{ev}_0]$ to $1$), and the right one is the one mentioned in \Cref{prop: omnibus graded k-theory}.8.
\begin{clm}
    $k=1$ in the above diagram.
\end{clm}
\begin{proof}
        We expand the diagram to 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: p circ ev0 claim}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} && {\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S})} && {\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} \\
	\mathbb Z && {\mathbb Z \oplus \mathbb Z} && \mathbb Z
	\arrow["{p_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev_0}_*}", from=1-3, to=1-5]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{(n,m) \mapsto n+m}", from=2-3, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
Observe that the right square commutes, as can be explicitly checked on the two generators $[\operatorname{id_\mathcal{S}}]$ and $[\alpha_{\mathcal{S}}]$. Furthermore, the rectangle
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} && {\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} \\
	\mathbb Z && \mathbb Z
	\arrow["{(\operatorname{ev}_0 \circ p)_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{n \mapsto 2n}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes too, as seen in \Cref{cor: ev0 circ p is mult by 2}. The claim follows.
\end{proof}
This also finishes the proof of the lemma.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- clm-2: body_md -->
$k=1$ in the above diagram.
<!-- end clm-2 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
We expand the diagram to 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: p circ ev0 claim}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} && {\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S})} && {\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} \\
	\mathbb Z && {\mathbb Z \oplus \mathbb Z} && \mathbb Z
	\arrow["{p_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{ev_0}_*}", from=1-3, to=1-5]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{(n,m) \mapsto n+m}", from=2-3, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
Observe that the right square commutes, as can be explicitly checked on the two generators $[\operatorname{id_\mathcal{S}}]$ and $[\alpha_{\mathcal{S}}]$. Furthermore, the rectangle
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} && {\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathcal{S},\mathbb C)} \\
	\mathbb Z && \mathbb Z
	\arrow["{(\operatorname{ev}_0 \circ p)_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{n \mapsto 2n}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes too, as seen in \Cref{cor: ev0 circ p is mult by 2}. The claim follows.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- cor-14: body_md -->
Let $A$ be a unital algebra in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$. The composite 
    \[
    {K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A) \xrightarrow{p^*} K_0^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_0^*} {K}^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}_0(A)
    \]
    maps the Fredholm cycle $(\mathcal{E},F) \in {K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A)$ to $(\mathcal{E} \oplus \mathcal{E},F \oplus (-F)) \in {K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A)$.
<!-- end cor-14 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
This follows from \Cref{lem: 1 plus x is the composition} and the formula of the explicit isomorphism $\pi_0{\mathbb{K}}^{\operatorname{G,sp}}(A) \cong {K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A)$ as mentioned in \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}.6.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- rem-24: body_md -->
\label{rem: simplify endo of K fr}
    Note that $(\mathcal{E},-F)$ is \emph{not} the inverse of $(\mathcal{E},F) \in {{K}}^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}_0(A)$; the usual formula of the inverse also requires to flip the grading on $\mathcal{E}$ (see \cite[Lemma 8.24]{D} for details). In fact, when $A$ is inner graded, $(\mathcal{E},-F)=(\mathcal{E},F)$, as can be seen from \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}.6. Thus, for inner graded $A$, ${K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A) \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_0^* \circ p^*} {K}_0^{G,\operatorname{Fr}}(A)$ is the multiplication by $2$ map.
<!-- end rem-24 -->
<!-- lem-16: body_md -->
\label{prop: j compose iota A triv graded over R}
    The diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A)} && {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(Cl^{1,0},A)} \\
	{\mathbb{K}^{G_2}(A)} && {\mathbb{K}^G(A_u)} 
	\arrow["{j^*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\simeq", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\simeq", from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{\mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G(-)}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes, where the left vertical equivalence is induced from \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}, and the right vertical equivalence is induced by \Cref{eqn: A inner graded over R}.  In particular, for unital $A$, the induced map $K_0^{G_2}(A) \rightarrow K_0^G(A)$ forgets the $C_2$-action on a $G_2$-equivariant projective $A$-module in $K_0^{G_2}(A)$.
<!-- end lem-16 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
In light of \Cref{lem: another description of j star}, we just need to show that the composite
    \[
    \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A) \xrightarrow{(A \rightarrow A \otimes Cl^{0,1})_*} \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A \otimes Cl^{0,1}) \xrightarrow[\cong]{\text{res}\dashv \text{coind}} \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}(\mathbb C,A_u)
    \]
    identifies with the restriction map. But this is clear in light of description of the counit of the restriction-coinduction adjunction as mentioned in \Cref{thm: adjunctions at kkg} (the adjunction holds good for non-separable algebras too).
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- prop-23: body_md -->
Let $A$ be an inner graded algebra in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$. Then, the fiber sequence in \Cref{eqn: dual fiber sequence} splits.
<!-- end prop-23 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
In light of \Cref{prop: j compose iota A triv graded over R}, it suffices to construct a section of the map $\mathbb{K}^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{res}^{G_2}_G(-)} \mathbb{K}^G(A_u)$. If $A$ were trivially graded, this section could have been taken to be $\mathsf{res}^G_{G_2}(-)$. In the general inner graded case, we use the fact that $A \simeq \operatorname{res}^{G}_{G_2}\operatorname{res}^{G_2}_GA$ in $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},\infty}$ as follows by an application of \cite[Example E.2.13]{WY} (see also \cite[Lemma 2.1]{BUNKEcrossed}).
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- cor-15: body_md -->
\label{cor: composition last ones}
Let $(A,\alpha)$ be a unital, inner graded algebra in $\mathsf G_2\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The composite $K_0^G(A_u) \xrightarrow{\iota^*} K_0^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{j^*} K_0^G(A_u)$ is given by
    \begin{align*}
        K_0^G(A_u) &\rightarrow K_0^G(A_u) \\
        [M] &\mapsto [M \oplus M_{\alpha}]=2[M]
    \end{align*}
    \item The composite $K_0^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{j^*} K_0^G(A_u) \xrightarrow{\iota^*} K_0^{G_2}(A)$ is given by
    \begin{align*}
    K_0^{G_2}(A) &\rightarrow K_0^{G_2}(A) \\
    [M,\alpha_M] &\mapsto[M \oplus M_{\alpha},\operatorname{flip}] = [M \oplus M, (m,n) \mapsto (\alpha_M(n),\alpha_M(m))]
    \end{align*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-15 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
Everything follows immediately from \Cref{cor: map induced by C in CL01} and \Cref{prop: j compose iota A triv graded over R}, except that we have to justify the equalities in Assertions 1 and 2. 
    
    For Assertion 1, it suffices to show that for $M$ a $G$-equivariant $A_u$-module over an inner graded $A$, then $M_\alpha \cong M$ as $G$-equivariant $A_u$-modules. If $u$ is the symmetry implementing the grading on $A$, then 
    \[
    M_{\alpha} \rightarrow M, ~~~ \underline{m} \mapsto mu
    \]
    is such an isomorphism.
    
    For Assertion 2, we first show that when $M$ is a $G_2$-equivariant projective $A$-module, then $M \cong M_{\alpha}$ as $G$-equivariant $A_u$-modules. Indeed, an isomorphism is given by 
    \begin{align*}
        M &\rightarrow M_\alpha \\
        m &\mapsto \underline{\alpha_M(m)}
    \end{align*}
    Under this isomorphism, $[M \oplus M_{\alpha},\operatorname{flip}]=[M \oplus M, (m,n) \mapsto (\alpha_M(n),\alpha_M(m))] \in K_0^{G_2}(A)$. Also compare the proof of \Cref{cor: map induced by C in CL01}.\footnote{actually this argument did not use that $A$ is inner graded, see also \Cref{cor: endomorphisms in the complex graded case}.}
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- lem-17: body_md -->
The diagram 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,A)} && {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(Cl^{1,0},A)} \\
	&& {\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(Cl^{0,1},A)} \\
	{K_0^{G_2}(A)} && {K_0^G(A_u)}
	\arrow["{j^*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\cong"', from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\cong", from=3-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{\text{forget $C_2$ action}}", from=3-1, to=3-3]
	\arrow["\cong", from=3-3, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes, where the left vertical isomorphism is induced from \Cref{thm: Recovering classical K-theories from our stable inf cat gen}, and the other maps are as described above.\footnote{we use the same notations as in the Real case; this should not create any confusion.}
<!-- end lem-17 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
The commutativity of the upper right triangle follows from the commutativity up to homotopy of \Cref{eqn: cliffords}. The commutativity of the trapezoid follows from explicitly chasing the definitions, similar to the proof of \Cref{cor: map induced by C in CL01}.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- cor-16: body_md -->
\label{cor: endomorphisms in the complex graded case}
    Let $(A,\alpha)$ be a unital, complex $G \times C_2$-equivariant complex $C^*$-algebra.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The composite $K_0^G(A_u) \xrightarrow{\iota^*} K_0^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{j^*} K_0^G(A_u)$ is given by
    \begin{align*}
        K_0^G(A_u) &\rightarrow K_0^G(A_u) \\
        [M] &\mapsto [M \oplus M_{\alpha}]
    \end{align*}
    \item The composite $K_0^{G_2}(A) \xrightarrow{j^*} K_0^G(A_u) \xrightarrow{\iota^*} K_0^{G_2}(A)$ is given by
    \begin{align*}
    K_0^{G_2}(A) &\rightarrow K_0^{G_2}(A) \\
    [M,\alpha_M] &\mapsto[M \oplus M_{\alpha},\operatorname{flip}] = [M \oplus M, (m,n) \mapsto (\alpha_M(n),\alpha_M(m))]
    \end{align*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-16 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
Exactly the same proof as \Cref{cor: composition last ones}.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- rem-25: body_md -->
We also mention another description of the map $K_0^{G_2}(A) \rightarrow K_0^{G_2}(A)$ as in \Cref{cor: endomorphisms in the complex graded case}.2. Using the isomorphism
    $
    Cl^{1,0} \cong Cl^{0,1}
    $, we can treat the composition 
    \[
    \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,A) \xrightarrow{j^*} \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(Cl^{1,0},A) \simeq \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(Cl^{0,1},A) \xrightarrow{\iota^*} \mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,A)
    \]
    as the $\mathrm{KK}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}$ product by the image under $\operatorname{res}^{C_2}_{G_2}$ of a certain element in $\mathrm{KK}^{C_2}_{\mathrm{ex},0}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)$. It turns out that this element is\footnote{we omit the details since it is not really needed anywhere} $(1,1)$, whence the induced map must be
    \begin{align*}
       K_0^{G_2}(A) &\rightarrow K_0^{G_2}(A)  \\
       [M,\alpha_M] &\mapsto [M \oplus M^{\operatorname{op}},\alpha_M \oplus (-\alpha_{M})]
    \end{align*}
    And indeed, we have an isomorphism of $G_2$-equivariant $A$-modules
    \begin{align*}
        M \oplus M_\alpha &\rightarrow M \oplus M^{\operatorname{op}}\\
        (m,\underline{n}) &\mapsto (\frac{m+\alpha_M(n)}{2},\frac{m-\alpha_M(n)}{2}).
    \end{align*}
    Thus, we actually have isomorphisms of $G_2$-equivariant $A$-modules
    \[
    (M \oplus M^{\operatorname{op}},\alpha_M \oplus (-\alpha_{M})) \cong (M \oplus M_{\alpha},\operatorname{flip})\cong (M \oplus M, (m,n) \mapsto (\alpha_M(n),\alpha_M(n))).
    \]
<!-- end rem-25 -->
<!-- rem-26: body_md -->
Note that when $A$ is a non-inner graded $C^*$-algebra, the fiber sequence in \Cref{eqn: dual fiber sequence} need not split. A concrete counterexample is $A=\mathbb{C}l^{1}$, since $K_0^{C_2}(\mathbb{C}l^{1}) \cong \mathbb Z$ (\Cref{prop: KOC2 CL01}) and $K_0(\mathbb{C}l^{3}_u)\cong K_0(\mathbb{C}l^{1}_u)\cong \mathbb Z \oplus \mathbb Z$.
<!-- end rem-26 -->
<!-- thm-11: body_md -->
{(Higson-Meyer-Thomsen)}\label{thm: HMT}
    The functor $\mathrm{kk}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ is initial among functors to an additive $1$-category which are reduced, homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable and split exact.
<!-- end thm-11 -->
<!-- rem-27: body_md -->
\label{rem: KKAS properties}
    The following remarks about Kasparov's $KK^G$-theory are in order
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item It is a deep result of Kasparov (\cite[Theorem 2.9]{KASEQQUIVARIANT}) that $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ has countable coproducts, and the functor $\mathrm{kk}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ takes countable direct sums in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to countable coproducts in $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$. An alternative proof using the Cuntz-Meyer picture of $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ can be given following \cite[Corollary 11.16]{KKandE}. 
        \item One can view the additive $1$-category $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ as a half exact additive category by taking the maximal marking and taking the distinguished half exact sequences to be all short exact sequences in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ admitting a equivariant cpc-split; the verification that this indeed is a half exact structure follows from \cite[Section 7]{BS} (see also \cite[Theorem 3.28]{ECH} and the discussion above it).
        \item $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ is a symmetric monoidal category and the functor $\mathrm{kk}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ has a symmetric monoidal refinement for both the minimal and the maximal tensor products on $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$; this is explicitly stated in \cite[Theorem 4.a]{CuntzBiv}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end rem-27 -->
<!-- thm-12: body_md -->
\label{thm: hoKK inf is KKKas}
    We have a natural equivalence of additive, symmetric monoidal (for both symmetric monoidal refinements) categories
    \[
    \mathrm{KK}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{se},0} \simeq \mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}.
    \]
<!-- end thm-12 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
By construction, the canonical functor 
    \[
    \mathrm{kk}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{se},0}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{se},0}
    \]
    is reduced, homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable, and additive. Thus, \Cref{thm: HMT} says that there exists a unique additive functor $\mathcal{F}: \mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{se},0}$ such that $\mathcal{F} \circ \mathrm{kk}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}} = \mathrm{kk}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{se},0}$.

On the other hand, the canonical functor \[
\mathrm{kk}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}
\]
is clearly reduced, homotopy invariant and ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable, as can be read off from \Cref{thm: HMT}. That it also satisfies the other hypothesis asked for in \Cref{prop: uni prop hoKK one categorical} is the content of \Cref{rem: KKAS properties}. We thus obtain a unique functor $\mathcal{G}: \mathrm{KK}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{se},0} \rightarrow \mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ such that $\mathcal{G} \circ \mathrm{kk}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{se},0} = \mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$. $\mathcal{G}$ is furthermore symmetric monoidal, as follows from the proof of \Cref{prop: uni prop hoKK one categorical} and \cite[Proposition 3.3.2]{HIN}. Our thesis now follows from a standard yoga with universal functors.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- rem-28: body_md -->
We implicitly used in the above proof the following basic facts: If $\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}$ are additive (resp. symmetric monoidal) categories, and $F: \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \mathcal{D}$ is an additive (resp. symmetric monoidal) functor which is an equivalence of the underlying categories, then the inverse is automatically additive (resp. symmetric monoidal).
<!-- end rem-28 -->
<!-- prop-24: body_md -->
\label{cor: KK large same}
    For $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$, we have a natural isomorphism of abelian groups
    \[
    \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{Kas}}(A,B) \cong \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},0}(A,B).
    \]
<!-- end prop-24 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
In light of \Cref{prop: ind omnibus}, we have for $A$ and $B$ as in the statement of this proposition, an equivalence (with notation as in \Cref{defi: s finitary}) of spectra
    \begin{align*}
        \operatorname{colim}_{B' \subseteq_{\operatorname{sep}} B}
        \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},\infty}\bigl(\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},\infty}(A),\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},\infty}(B')\bigr)
        \xrightarrow{\simeq}
        \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},\infty}\bigl(\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},\infty}(A),\mathrm{kk}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},\infty}(B)\bigr)
    \end{align*}
    Since homotopy groups of spectra commute with filtered colimits, our thesis follows from the classical result that
    \[
    \operatorname{colim}_{B' \subseteq_{\operatorname{sep}} B}
    \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{Kas}}(A,B')
    \xrightarrow{\cong}
    \mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{Kas}}(A,B),
    \]
    see for example \cite[Lemma 2.1]{AZZA}.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- rem-29: body_md -->
\label{rem: KK SKA}
    When the $C^*$-algebra $A$ in the first variable is not separable, $\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{se},0}(A,-)$ need not coincide with $\mathrm{KK}^{G}_{\mathrm{Kas}}(A,-)$ a'la Skandalis; it boils down to the issue that homotopy groups of homotopy limits need not be limits of homotopy groups.
<!-- end rem-29 -->
<!-- defi-19: body_md -->
\label{defi: e class preparation}
    \hfill
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 	Let $A,B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$. An asymptotic morphism
from $A$ to $B$ is a one-parameter family of functions $\varphi_t : A \to B$ with $t \in
[1, \infty)$, satisfying the continuity condition that for all $a \in
A$, the map
\[
t \longmapsto \varphi_t(a) : [1, \infty) \to B
\]
 is bounded and
continuous, and the asymptotic conditions that for all $a, a_1, a_2 \in A$ and
$\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ 
\[
\begin{rcases}
	\varphi_t(a_1a_2) -  \varphi_t(a_1)\varphi_t(a_2)\\
	\varphi_t(a_1+a_2)- \varphi_t(a_1) - \varphi_t(a_2)\\
	\varphi_t(\lambda a ) - \lambda \varphi_t(a)\\
	\varphi_t(a^{*}) - \varphi_t(a)^{*}\\
    \varphi_t(g.a)-g.\varphi_t(a)
\end{rcases}
\to 0, \qquad \text{as }t \to \infty
\]
When $A$ and $B$ are Real, we shall require that in addition
\[
\tau(\varphi_t(a)) - \varphi_t(\tau(a)) \to 0 \qquad \text{as }t
\to \infty.
\] 
We shall denote an
asymptotic morphism $\varphi : A
\dashrightarrow B$ with  a dashed arrow.
\item There is a natural notion of homotopy between asymptotic morphisms which is an equivalence relation (see \cite[Chapter 2]{HGT}), and we denote by $[[A,B]]_G$ the $G$-equivariant asymptotic homotopy classes of maps\footnote{as in the ordinary homotopy case, if the external group $G$ is clear from the context, we omit it from the notation.} from $A$ to $B$. This forms a category $\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$, whose objects are separable $G$-$C^*$-algebras, and morphisms are $G$-equivariant asymptotic homotopy classes of maps.
\item Just as the passage from $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}_{h}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ (see \Cref{prop: SKGRALKGseph omnibus}.1), one can form the category $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$ via left and right Bousfield localizations of $\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$, whose hom monoids would be ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stabilized asymptotic homotopy classes of maps.

Note that $\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$ and $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$ are $1$-categories; an $\infty$-categorical refinement of these categories has been studied in \cite{EisCASS} when $G$ is a discrete countable group. The methods of loc.\! cit.\! would not generalize to general locally compact second countable groups. We anyway work only with the $1$-categorical variants in this section.
\item The classical $E^G$-groups are given by
\[
\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B):=\operatorname{hom}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}}(\Omega A,\Omega B)=[[\Omega A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},\Omega B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]],
\]
and yield a symmetric monoidal additive category structure on $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ with respect to the maximal tensor product on $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$. That it indeed becomes a symmetric monoidal additive category can be seen by combining the approaches and relevant results of \cite{HGT} and \cite{BOERSEMA}. There is an obvious functor
\[
\mathrm{e}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}.
\]
\item One can view the additive $1$-category $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ as a half exact additive category by taking the maximal marking and taking the distinguished half exact sequences to be all short exact sequences in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$; see \Cref{lem: folklore lem}.3 for details. \emph{In the remainder of this subsection, we by default work with this half exact structure.} 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end defi-19 -->
<!-- lem-18: body_md -->
\label{lem: technical asy}
    Let $A,B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Denote by $\widetilde{[[A,B]]}$ the set of homotopy classes of asymptotic morphisms $\varphi: A \dashrightarrow B$ which have the property that $\varphi_1(a)=0 ~\forall~ a \in A$. Homotopies are also required to satisfy this condition. Then the natural map
    \[
    \Phi_{A,B}:\widetilde{[[A,B]]} \rightarrow [[A,B]]
    \]
    is an isomorphism.
<!-- end lem-18 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
We just write a map in the other direction; that it is well-defined and inverse to $\Phi_{A,B}$ is a routine check.

    Fix a function $f:[1,\infty) \rightarrow [0,1]$ with the property that $f(1)=0, f(t)=1~\forall~t \geq 2$. Then the pointwise multiplication of $f$ with an element of $[[A,B]]$ does the job.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- lem-19: body_md -->
\label{lem: HLT lemma}
    In the notation of the above discussion, let $\psi: \Omega A \dashrightarrow \Omega B$ be the asymptotic morphism obtained by applying the equivariant (Real) Connes-Higson construction (\cite[Proposition 5.5]{HGT}, \cite[Proposition 4.3]{BOERSEMA}) to the top extension in \Cref{eqn: E phi of thomsen}. Then $[\psi]=-[\Omega \varphi]$ in $[[\Omega A,\Omega B]]$.
<!-- end lem-19 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
This is the content of \cite[Lemma 1.3]{ThomsenLarsen}, see also \cite[Lemma 3.4]{THOASY}. Note that there is a sign error in the analogous assertion \cite[Proposition 5.12]{HGT}.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- thm-13: body_md -->
{(folklore)}\label{thm: folklore}
    The functor $\mathrm{e}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ is initial among functors to an additive $1$-category which are reduced, homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable and half exact.
<!-- end thm-13 -->
<!-- prop-25: body_md -->
\label{prop: asy split exact functor}
    For each $D \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, the functor $[[D,-]]: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \operatorname{Set}_*$ is split exact.
<!-- end prop-25 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
Let $0 \rightarrow A \rightarrow B \xrightarrow{f} C \rightarrow0$ be a short exact sequence in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ which is split by a homomorphism $\sigma: C \rightarrow B$. Without loss of generality, we can assume that the map $A \rightarrow B$ is the inclusion of an ideal. From the standard excision properties in the asymptotic category and Puppe sequences in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$,(\cite[Proposition 5.16]{HGT}, \cite[Proposition 2.5]{HG}), we get a long exact sequence of pointed sets
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn: les asy}
        ...\rightarrow [[D,\Omega B]] \xrightarrow{\Omega f_*}[[D,\Omega C]] \xrightarrow{\partial}[[D,C(f)]] \rightarrow [[D,B]] \xrightarrow{f_*} [[D,C]] \rightarrow 0
    \end{equation}
    where $C(f)$ denotes the mapping cone of $f$.
    Since $f$ is split by $\sigma$, $\Omega f$ is split by $\Omega \sigma$, and we can extract the split exact sequence
    \[
    0 \rightarrow [[D,C(f)]] \rightarrow [[D,B]] \xrightarrow{f_*} [[D,C]] \rightarrow 0
    \]
    from \Cref{eqn: les asy}. To prove our thesis, it therefore suffices to show that the inclusion $A \rightarrow C(f)$ is an isomorphism in $\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$.
    
    Using the split $\sigma$, we can re-write $C(f)$ as
    \[
    C(f)=\{(a+\sigma(\gamma(0)),\gamma)\mid a \in A\} \subseteq B \oplus PC.
    \]
    Let $u_t$ be a (Real) quasicentral approximate unit in $A$ (\cite[Lemma 5.3]{HGT}). In light of \cite[Lemma 5.6.(iii)]{HGT}, we can now define a $1$-parameter family of homomorphisms
    \begin{align*}
        \varphi_t: C_0(0,1] &\rightarrow A \\
        f &\mapsto f(u_t)
    \end{align*}
    given by functional calculi of the individual $u_t$. We can now define an asymptotic morphism given by the family of maps
    \begin{align*}
        \rho_t:C_0(0,1] \otimes C &\rightarrow A \\
        f \otimes c &\mapsto f(u_t)\sigma(c)
    \end{align*}
     Note that in defining it, we used the universal property of the maximal tensor product, see \cite[Section 25.2.3]{BLAK}. We can now define an asymptotic morphism $\varphi: C(f) \dashrightarrow A$ given by 
    \[
    \varphi_t(a+\sigma(\gamma(0)),\gamma)=a+\rho_t(f).
    \]
    The verification that it indeed is an inverse to the inclusion $A \rightarrow C(f)$ in $\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$ can now be taken from the proof of \cite[Proposition 3.2]{DL}. The equivariance and Real structure do not pose any additional difficulties.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lem-20: body_md -->
\label{lem: folklore lem}
    \hfill 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Let $F:\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathcal{D}$ be a functor to a half exact additive $1$-category which is homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable, half exact with respect to exact sequences. Then there is an isomorphism \[F(C_0(\mathbb R^{2,2}) \otimes A) \xrightarrow[\cong]{\operatorname{Bott}^F} F(A)\] which is natural with respect to morphisms in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and also with respect to the boundary maps of the long exact sequence associated to $F$, as described in \cite[Theorem 21.4.4]{BLAK}.
        \item The natural map
        \[
        C_0(\mathbb R^{0,1}) \otimes -: \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B) \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(\Omega A, \Omega B)
        \]
        is an isomorphism.
        \item The functor $\mathrm{e}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}: \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ is homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable, and half exact.
        \item The natural map
        \[
        C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0}) \otimes -: \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B) \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0}) \otimes A, C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0}) \otimes B)
        \]
        is an isomorphism.
        \item The isomorphisms of Assertion 1 applied to the functors $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,-)$ and $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(-,C_0(\mathbb R^{2,2}) \otimes B)$ fit into a commutative diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	&& {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(C_0(\mathbb R^{2,2}) \otimes A, C_0(\mathbb R^{2,2}) \otimes B)} \\
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,B)} && {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A, C_0(\mathbb R^{2,2}) \otimes B)}
	\arrow["\cong", no head, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{C_0(\mathbb R^{2,2}) \otimes -}"{pos=0.4}, no head, from=2-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\cong"', no head, from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-20 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
We begin with Assertion 1. In light of the given properties of $F$, the Real analog of the proof of \cite[Proposition 6.16]{HGT} shows that there exists an asymptotic morphism \[\alpha:C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \dashrightarrow \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)\] 
such that for each $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, the asymptotic morphism
\[
\alpha \otimes 1_A:C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes A\dashrightarrow \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N) \otimes A
\]
yields a natural isomorphism
\[
F(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes A) \xrightarrow[\cong]{\operatorname{Bott}_A^F} F(A).
\]
Our sought after natural map is now obtained by applying the above isomorphism twice
\[
F(C_0(\mathbb R^{2,2}) \otimes A) \xrightarrow[\cong]{\operatorname{Bott}_{C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes A}^F} F(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes A) \xrightarrow[\cong]{\operatorname{Bott}_{A}^F} F(A).
\]\\
  The map in Assertion 2 being an isomorphism can be readily taken from \cite[Lemma 4.5]{BOERSEMA}, with the obvious modifications to tackle the equivariant case. \\\\
    We now prove Assertion 3 (note that it settles the easy part of \Cref{thm: folklore}). That $\mathrm{e}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ is homotopy invariant and ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable is obvious. That it is also half exact follows by combining \cite[Theorem 4.4]{BOERSEMA} and the excision theory of equivariant $E$-theory developed in chapters 5 and 6 of \cite{HGT}. The careful reader will observe that (variants of) Assertions 1 and 2 go as an input to proving the exactness in the first variable in \cite{BOERSEMA} and \cite{HGT}.\\\\
    For Assertion 4, we can accommodate the map in the commutative diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{E^{G}_{\operatorname{class}}(A,B)} && {E^{G}_{\operatorname{class}}(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes A,C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes B)} \\
