	& {E^{G}_{\operatorname{class}}(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0})\otimes A,C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0})\otimes B)}
	\arrow["{C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes -}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0}) \otimes -}"'{pos=0.2}, from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{C_0(\mathbb R^{0,1}) \otimes -}"'{pos=0.8}, from=2-2, to=1-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
The discussion preceding the lemma shows that the horizontal arrow is an isomorphism, since \[C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \simeq_{\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}} \mathbb{C}.\]The right arrow is an isomorphism from Assertion 2.\\\\
Finally we show Assertion 5. In light of Assertion 1, it essentially follows from the commutativity of the diagram                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes A} && {\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N) \otimes A} \\
	{C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes B} && {\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N) \otimes B}
	\arrow["{\alpha \otimes 1_A}", dashed, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{1_{C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})} \otimes f}"', dashed, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{1_{\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)} \otimes f}", dashed, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\alpha \otimes 1_B}", dashed, from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
for every asympototic morphism $f: A \dashrightarrow B$, as can be seen from the symmetric monoidal properties of $\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$. See also \cite[Theorem 4.6]{HGT} and the proof of \cite[Proposition 6.16]{HGT}.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- cor-17: body_md -->
\label{cor: Bott inverted}
    There exists an asymptotic morphism $\alpha:C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\dashrightarrow \mathcal{K}(l^2)$ such that \[\alpha \otimes 1_B: C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes B \dashrightarrow \mathcal{K}(l^2) \otimes B\] determines an invertible class in $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes B,B)$. Furthermore, the functor 
    \[
    \Omega: \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G} \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}
    \]
    exhibits $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ as the $1$-categorical localization of $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$ at the classes of maps $\alpha \otimes 1_B$.
<!-- end cor-17 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
The first statement follows readily from the proof of Assertion 1 of \Cref{lem: folklore lem} by taking $\mathcal{D}=\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$. The second statement follows from the following general fact about $(\infty-)$categories (it is the dual version of \cite[Proposition 5.2.7.4]{HTT}) : Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category with an endofunctor $R: \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$ and a natural transformation $\mathfrak{T}: R \implies \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{C}}$. If for every object $C \in \mathcal{C}$ the morphims
    \[
    \mathfrak{T}_{R(C)},R(\mathfrak{T}_C): R(R(C)) \rightarrow R(C)
    \]
    are equivalences, then $R:\mathcal{C} \rightarrow R\mathcal{C}$ is the right-adjoint of a right Bousfield localization with counit $\mathfrak{T}$. It is also the Dwyer-Kan localization at the set of morphisms $W_R:=\{\mathfrak{T}_C \mid C \in \mathcal{C}\}$. 

    Indeed, in the above notation, take $\mathcal{C}:=\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$, and $R:= C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes - :\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G} \rightarrow \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$. The rest follows from the results of \Cref{lem: folklore lem} and the definition of $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- prop-26: body_md -->
{(cf. \cite[Theorem 4.6]{THOASY})}\label{prop: thomsen heart}
    Let $F$ be a homotopy invariant, ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stable and half exact functor from $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to $\operatorname{Ab}$. Fix $A$ in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and consider an arbitrary element $d \in F(A)$. Then there is a unique natural transformation 
    \[
    T: \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,-) \implies F(-)
    \]
    such that $T_A([\operatorname{id}_A])=d$.
<!-- end prop-26 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
Firstly, we massage the hom groups of $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ a bit, and write them as
    \[
    \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B)=[[C_0(\mathbb R^{2,1}) \otimes A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},  C_0(\mathbb R^{2,1}) \otimes B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]].
    \]
    Indeed this can be done from Assertions 2 and 4 of \Cref{lem: folklore lem} (the reason we do this maneuver will be clear from the upcoming proof, but see also \Cref{rem: why not one zero}).

    \textit{To avoid notational clutter, we subsequently denote $C_0(\mathbb R^{p,q}) \otimes X$ as $\mathbb R^{p,q}X$ for any $X \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Same comment applies to functors involving these algebras.}
    
    Now consider $x \in [[\mathbb R^{2,1} A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},  \mathbb R^{2,1}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]]$. Let it be represented by the equivariant asymptotic morphism 
    \[
    \varphi: \mathbb R^{2,1}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G} \dashrightarrow \mathbb R^{2,1}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}.
    \]
     As in \Cref{eqn: E phi of thomsen}, this yields an extension
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn: thomsen proof}
        0 \rightarrow \mathbb R^{2,2}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G} \rightarrow P_\varphi \rightarrow \mathbb R^{2,1}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G} \rightarrow 0.
    \end{equation}
    Consequently, we obtain a morphism $F(\mathbb R^{2,2}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G} ) \rightarrow F(\mathbb R^{2,2}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G} )$ in $\operatorname{Ab}$ via the connecting map of the long exact sequence associated to $F$ as in \cite[Theorem 21.4.4]{BLAK}. The ${\mathcal{K}_G}$-stability of $F$ together with Assertion 1 of \Cref{lem: folklore lem} naturally produces a morphism $T_x: F(A) \rightarrow F(B)$. Now define
    \begin{align*}
        T_B: [[\mathbb R^{2,1}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},  \mathbb R^{2,1}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]] \rightarrow F(B) \\
        x \mapsto T_x(d).
    \end{align*}
    In light of the machinery we developed in this subsection and functoriality properties of the Connes-Higson construction, the well-definedness and naturality of $T_B$, as well as the verification $T_A([\operatorname{id}_A])=d$ is a routine check, as has been done in the proof of \cite[Theorem 4.6]{THOASY}.

    We now prove the uniqueness part. Let 
    \[
    T':[[\mathbb R^{2,1}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},  \mathbb R^{2,1}- \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]] \rightarrow F(-)
    \]
    be a natural transformation such that $T'([\operatorname{id}_A])=d$. Consider $x =[\varphi] \in [[\mathbb R^{2,1}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},  \mathbb R^{2,1}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]]$. Let $\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3,\partial_4$ denote the connecting maps obtained by applying the functors \[[[\mathbb R^{4,3}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}, \mathbb R^{2,1}- ]], [[\mathbb R^{2,1}A\otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}, \mathbb R^{2,1}-]], F(\mathbb R^{2,2} -), F(-)\] respectively to the extension in \Cref{eqn: thomsen proof}\footnote{denoting by $\mathcal{G}$ any one of these four functors, we are implicitly using the natural identification of $\mathcal{G}(-)$ with $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb R^{2,2}\otimes {\mathcal{K}_G} \otimes -)$ in what follows.}. We get a commutative diagram
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: thomsen dia}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\begin{tikzcd}
	&& {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A,\mathbb R^{2,2}A)} & {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A,\mathbb R^{2,2}B)} && \\
	\\
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,A)} && {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,\mathbb R^{2,2}A)} & {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A, \mathbb R^{2,2}B)} && {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,B)} \\
	&& {F(\mathbb R^{2,2}A)} & {F(\mathbb R^{2,2}B)} \\
	&& {F(A)} & {F(B)}
	\arrow["{\partial_1}", color={rgb,255:red,92;green,92;blue,214}, from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{Bott}^{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(-,\mathbb R^{2,2}A)}}"{description}, no head, from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{Bott}^{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(-,\mathbb R^{2,2}B)}}"{description}, no head, from=1-4, to=3-4]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{2,2}-}", shift left, color={rgb,255:red,92;green,92;blue,214}, from=3-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{Bott}^{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,-)}}"', no head, from=3-1, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{T'_A}"', from=3-1, to=5-3]
	\arrow["{\partial_2}", from=3-3, to=3-4]
	\arrow["{T'_{\mathbb R^{2,2}A}}", from=3-3, to=4-3]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{Bott}^{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,-)}}"', no head, from=3-4, to=3-6]
	\arrow["{T'_{\mathbb R^{2,2}B}}", from=3-4, to=4-4]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{2,2}-}"', shift right, color={rgb,255:red,92;green,92;blue,214}, from=3-6, to=1-4]
	\arrow["{T'_B}", from=3-6, to=5-4]
	\arrow["{\partial_3}", from=4-3, to=4-4]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{Bott}^F}", no head, from=4-3, to=5-3]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{Bott}^F}", no head, from=4-4, to=5-4]
	\arrow["{\partial_4}", from=5-3, to=5-4]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
where the undirected edges are induced by the maps described in \Cref{lem: folklore lem}.1. Note that the fact that the diagram indeed commutes needs a lot of the machinery we developed earlier in this subsection.

We now claim the following.
\begin{clm}
    The composite 
    \[
    \partial_1 \circ (\mathbb R^{2,2}-) : \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,A) \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A, \mathbb R^{2,2}B)
    \]
    equals the composite
    \[
    (\mathbb R^{2,2}-) \circ \varphi_* :\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,A) \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A, \mathbb R^{2,2}B).
    \]
\end{clm}
\begin{proof}
    We build the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A,\mathbb R^{2,2}A)} &&&& {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A,\mathbb R^{2,2}B)} \\
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,1}A,\mathbb R^{2,1}A)} &&&& {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,1}A,\mathbb R^{2,1}B)} \\
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,0}A,\mathbb R^{2,0}A)} &&&& {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,0}A,\mathbb R^{2,0}B)} \\
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,A)} &&&& {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A,B)}
	\arrow["{\partial_1}", from=1-1, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{0,1}-}"', from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{-\partial_{[[\mathbb R^{4,2}A \otimes \mathcal{K}_G, \mathbb R^{2,0}- \otimes \mathcal{K}_G]]}}", from=2-1, to=2-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{0,1}-}", from=2-5, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{0,1}-}"', from=3-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{(\mathbb R^{2,0}\varphi)_*}", from=3-1, to=3-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{0,1}-}", from=3-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{2,0}-}"', from=4-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{\varphi_*}", from=4-1, to=4-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{2,0}-}", from=4-5, to=3-5]
\end{tikzcd}\]
We need to show that it commutes. The bottom rectangle commutes by the symmetric monoidal properties of $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$. The middle rectangle commutes by an application of \Cref{lem: HLT lemma}, together with the fact that composition with the Connes-Higson morphism yields the boundary map in $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$, as described in \cite[Theorem 6.15]{HGT}. The top square commuting is a consequence of the general fact that for any $A',B',C' \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $\psi \in \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(B',C')$, the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\Omega A',\Omega B')} && {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\Omega B',\Omega C')} \\
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A',B')} && {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(B',C')}
	\arrow["{-\Omega\psi_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\Omega_*}"', from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{\psi_*}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\Omega_*}", from=2-3, to=1-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
commutes. This boils down to the fact that the map $S^1 \wedge S^1 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{flip}} S^1 \wedge S^1$ has degree $-1$.

\end{proof}
The above claim therefore shows that the composite of the purple arrows (we are reversing the direction of the last arrow so as to compose) maps $[\operatorname{id}_A] \in \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,A)$ to $[\varphi] \in \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B)$. The commutativity of \Cref{eqn: thomsen dia} now tells that 
\[
\partial_4(T_A'([\operatorname{id}_A]))= T_B'([\varphi]).
\]
Since $T_A'([\operatorname{id}_A])$ is given to be $d$, the proof of the proposition follows.
<!-- end proof-71 -->

    \]
    equals the composite
    \[
    (\mathbb R^{2,2}-) \circ \varphi_* :\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,A) \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A, \mathbb R^{2,2}B).

	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A,\mathbb R^{2,2}A)} &&&& {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb R^{2,2}A,\mathbb R^{2,2}B)} \\

	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{0,1}-}", from=3-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{2,0}-}"', from=4-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{\varphi_*}", from=4-1, to=4-5]
	\arrow["{\mathbb R^{2,0}-}", from=4-5, to=3-5]
\end{tikzcd}\]
We need to show that it commutes. The bottom rectangle commutes by the symmetric monoidal properties of $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$. The middle rectangle commutes by an application of \Cref{lem: HLT lemma}, together with the fact that composition with the Connes-Higson morphism yields the boundary map in $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$, as described in \cite[Theorem 6.15]{HGT}. The top square commuting is a consequence of the general fact that for any $A',B',C' \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $\psi \in \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(B',C')$, the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\Omega A',\Omega B')} && {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(\Omega B',\Omega C')} \\
	{E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(A',B')} && {E^G_{\operatorname{class}}(B',C')}
	\arrow["{-\Omega\psi_*}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\Omega_*}"', from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["{\psi_*}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\Omega_*}", from=2-3, to=1-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
commutes. This boils down to the fact that the map $S^1 \wedge S^1 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{flip}} S^1 \wedge S^1$ has degree $-1$.

<!-- rem-30: body_md -->
\label{rem: why not one zero}
    In the above proof, $(2,2)$-periodicity played a crucial role. It would indeed be natural to expect that the same could be done by the more standard $(1,1)$-periodicity. Unraveling the proof of \Cref{prop: thomsen heart}, one would then want to take 
    \[
    \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B)=[[\mathbb R^{1,0}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}, \mathbb R^{1,0}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]].
    \]
    But it is not clear why this definition coincides with $[[\mathbb R^{0,1}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}, \mathbb R^{0,1}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]]$: the results of \Cref{lem: folklore lem} do not say this! Tracing further back, the reader may wonder ``why not \emph{define} $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B):=[[\mathbb R^{1,0}A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}, \mathbb R^{1,0}B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]]$?" The reason is that then it would not be clear why this category has excision; the development of the excision results in $E$-theory and the Connes-Higson morphism depend on Puppe sequences, where the loops are $C_0(\mathbb R^{0,1})$ and not $C_0(\mathbb R^{1,0})$.
<!-- end rem-30 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
With \Cref{prop: thomsen heart} at our disposal, the argument now follows by  standard yoga with the uniqueness of the natural transformations described in loc.\! cit.\! See for example \cite[Theorem 4.5]{HIGFIRST}. A few more details on a similar line of ideas is in \cite[Theorem 4.9]{THOASY}.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- thm-14: body_md -->
\label{thm: hoKKex is Eclass}
    We have a natural equivalence of additive, symmetric monoidal categories 
    \[
    \mathrm{KK}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}_{\mathrm{ex},0} \simeq \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}.
    \]
<!-- end thm-14 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
The proof of \Cref{thm: hoKK inf is KKKas} can be readily adapted to this case. The main check one needs to make is that $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ has countable coproducts, and the functor $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ takes countable direct sums in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to countable coproducts in $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$. But this is the content of \cite[Proposition 7.1]{HGT}. The Real structure poses no additional difficulty.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- thm-15: body_md -->
{(Generalized Dadarlat-Loring)}\label{thm: Gen DL}
    Let $A \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Suppose that for all $B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ the abelian monoid
    \[
    \operatorname{hom}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}}(A,B)=[[A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]]
    \]
    is a group. Then, the map
    \[
    \Omega:  [[A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}, B \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]] \rightarrow \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B)
    \]
    is an isomorphism of abelian groups for all $B \in \mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.
<!-- end thm-15 -->
<!-- rem-31: body_md -->
An $A$ in $\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ satisfying the hypothesis of the above theorem is called \emph{homotopy symmetric}. Note that it is equivalent to asking that the abelian monoid $[[A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G},A \otimes {\mathcal{K}_G}]]$ is a group.
<!-- end rem-31 -->
<!-- prop-27: body_md -->
\label{prop: prop for GDL}
    For each homotopy symmetric $A \in \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$, the functor
    \[
    \operatorname{hom}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}}(A,-):\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}
    \]
    inverts $\alpha: C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \dashrightarrow \mathcal{K}(l^2)$.
<!-- end prop-27 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
In light of \Cref{prop: asy split exact functor} and the universal property of $KK^G_{\operatorname{Kas}}$, there is a unique dashed arrow rendering the below diagram commutative.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: hom asy factor through KK}
\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathsf G\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}} & {\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}} &&& {\operatorname{Ab}} \\
	& {\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\mathrm{kk}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}}"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\operatorname{hom}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}}(A,-)}", from=1-2, to=1-5]
	\arrow[dashed, from=2-2, to=1-5]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
We now momentarily ignore the external group $G$. Since $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{\mathrm{sep}}$  satisfies $(1,1)$-periodicity, we know in light of the Cuntz picture of $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ that there is a morphism $q\mathbb C \xrightarrow{\beta} C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes \mathcal{K}(l^2)$ in $\mathsf C^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^\mathrm{sep}$ which implements the $(1,1)$-periodicity. There is also a homomorphism $q\mathbb C \xrightarrow{\gamma} \mathcal{K}$ given by the composite
\[
q\mathbb C \xrightarrow{\pi_1} \mathbb C \xrightarrow{\iota} \mathcal{K}(l^2).
\]
We now claim the following.
\begin{clm}
    The diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\begin{equation}\label{eqn: alpha beta gamma}
    \begin{tikzcd}
	{q\mathbb{C}} && {\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb{N})} \\
	& {C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb{N})}
	\arrow["\gamma", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\beta"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\alpha"', dashed, from=2-2, to=1-3]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
commutes upto a sign in the $\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)$-stabilized asymptotic homotopy category $L_\mathcal{K}\!\operatorname{Asy}$.
\end{clm}
\begin{proof}
    We consider the following diagram, where the vertical maps are induced by the localization functor $L_\mathcal{K}\!\operatorname{Asy} \rightarrow E_{\operatorname{class}}$ (i.e. the trivial group case of \Cref{cor: Bott inverted}).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
\[
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
[[q\mathbb{C},C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]]
&
\times
&
[[C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N),\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]]
&
\longrightarrow
&
[[q\mathbb{C},\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]]\cong\mathbb Z
\\[1.2ex]
\downarrow
&&
\downarrow
&&
\downarrow\scriptstyle{\cong}
\\[1.2ex]
E_{\operatorname{class}}
\bigl(q\mathbb{C},C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)\bigr)
&
\times
&
E_{\operatorname{class}}
\bigl(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N),
\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)\bigr)
&
\longrightarrow
&
E_{\operatorname{class}}
\bigl(q\mathbb{C},\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)\bigr)\cong\mathbb Z
\\[0.5ex]
\cong \mathbb Z
&&
\cong \mathbb Z
&&
\end{array}
$}
\]
We now justify the isomorphisms appearing on the diagram. That $[[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]] \cong \mathbb Z$ follows from 
\[
\mathbb Z \xrightarrow[\cong]{\Cref{prop: Cuntz picture k-theory}} [q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)] \xrightarrow[\cong]{\Cref{rem: qA properties}.6} [[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]].
\]
 We furthermore note that $\gamma$ corresponds to $1$ under this isomorphism; see \Cref{rem: the map in the cuntz picture iso}. The isomorphisms in the bottom row follow since $q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N), C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})$ are all $KK_{\operatorname{Kas}}^{\operatorname{sep}}$-equivalent to $\mathbb C$, and $K_0(\mathbb C) \cong \mathbb Z$. That the right vertical map is an isomorphism follows from the composite map
\[
[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)] \xrightarrow{\cong} [[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]] \rightarrow E_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)
\]
being an isomorphism from \Cref{lem: qC special} (we are implicitly also using the universal property of $\mathcal{K}(l^2)$-stabilized homotopy category of separable $C^*$-algebras here). From the discussion preceding the claim, $\beta$ and $\alpha$ map to a generator in $\mathbb Z$ under the two left vertical arrows. An argument similar to the one in \Cref{lem: product of bott elements iso} shows that the bottom bilinear map must send $1 \times 1$ to $\pm 1$. The conclusion follows.
\end{proof}
We are now in a position to bring back the group $G$. Since all the algebras in \Cref{eqn: alpha beta gamma} have the trivial $G$-action, we conclude that \Cref{eqn: alpha beta gamma} also commutes in $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$. Furthermore, $\gamma$ and $\beta$ remain equivalences in $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$, whence so is $\alpha$. The proof of the proposition follows in light of \Cref{eqn: hom asy factor through KK}.
<!-- end proof-75 -->

	& {C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb{N})}
	\arrow["\gamma", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\beta"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\alpha"', dashed, from=2-2, to=1-3]

E_{\operatorname{class}}
\bigl(C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})\otimes\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N),
\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)\bigr)
&
\longrightarrow
&
E_{\operatorname{class}}
\bigl(q\mathbb{C},\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)\bigr)\cong\mathbb Z
\\[0.5ex]
\cong \mathbb Z
&&
\cong \mathbb Z
&&
\end{array}
$}
\]
We now justify the isomorphisms appearing on the diagram. That $[[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]] \cong \mathbb Z$ follows from 
\[
\mathbb Z \xrightarrow[\cong]{\Cref{prop: Cuntz picture k-theory}} [q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)] \xrightarrow[\cong]{\Cref{rem: qA properties}.6} [[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]].
\]
 We furthermore note that $\gamma$ corresponds to $1$ under this isomorphism; see \Cref{rem: the map in the cuntz picture iso}. The isomorphisms in the bottom row follow since $q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N), C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1})$ are all $KK_{\operatorname{Kas}}^{\operatorname{sep}}$-equivalent to $\mathbb C$, and $K_0(\mathbb C) \cong \mathbb Z$. That the right vertical map is an isomorphism follows from the composite map
\[
[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)] \xrightarrow{\cong} [[q\mathbb C,\mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N)]] \rightarrow E_{\operatorname{class}}(\mathbb C,\mathbb C)
\]
being an isomorphism from \Cref{lem: qC special} (we are implicitly also using the universal property of $\mathcal{K}(l^2)$-stabilized homotopy category of separable $C^*$-algebras here). From the discussion preceding the claim, $\beta$ and $\alpha$ map to a generator in $\mathbb Z$ under the two left vertical arrows. An argument similar to the one in \Cref{lem: product of bott elements iso} shows that the bottom bilinear map must send $1 \times 1$ to $\pm 1$. The conclusion follows.
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
In light of \Cref{cor: Bott inverted} and general facts about mapping spaces (in our context, mapping abelian groups) out of colocal objects (\cite[Remark 9.9]{KKandE}), it suffices to show that the functor 
    \[
    \operatorname{hom}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}}(A,-): \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}
    \]
    inverts the morphisms $\alpha \otimes 1_B: C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes B \dashrightarrow \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N) \otimes B$. But this follows upon tensoring \Cref{eqn: alpha beta gamma} with $B$; the diagram continues to commute up to a sign (which is independent of $B$), and the morphisms $q\mathbb C \otimes B \xrightarrow{\beta \otimes 1_B} C_0(\mathbb R^{1,1}) \otimes \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N) \otimes  B$ and $q\mathbb C \otimes B \xrightarrow{\gamma \otimes 1_B} \mathcal{K}(l^2\mathbb N) \otimes B$ are isomorphisms in $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$.
<!-- end proof-77 -->
<!-- rem-32: body_md -->
The following remarks about \Cref{thm: Gen DL} are in order.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There is a non-technical way to think about the result. Note that \Cref{cor: Bott inverted} roughly says that one obtains $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ from $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$ by ``inverting Bott". When $A$ is homotopy symmetric, \Cref{eqn: hom asy factor through KK} shows that the functor \[\operatorname{hom}_{\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}}(A,-): \mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G} \rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}\] indeed ``inverts Bott", since it factors through $\mathrm{KK}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$. \Cref{prop: prop for GDL} basically makes this line of argument rigorous. And probably this is also the argument which was hinted at the end of Section 4 in \cite{DL}.
        \item A treatment analogous to Section 3.4 would now show that $\mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ is the full subcategory of group objects of $\mathrm S_{{\mathcal{K}_G}}\operatorname{Asy}^{G}$. This seems to not have been mentioned in the literature.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end rem-32 -->
<!-- defi-20: body_md -->
{(cf. \cite[Chapter 2]{HG})}
    For $A,B \in \mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, define a category $\widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ with objects the objects of $\mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}$, and morphims from $A$ to $B$ being given by 
    \[
    \widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B):=[[\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G, B \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G]]_{\operatorname{gr}}.
    \]
    The composition law in $\widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ is given by the usual formula (see \cite[Definition 2.9]{HG}) using the codiagonal map $\mathcal{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathcal{S} \hat\otimes \mathcal{S}$. Denote by
    \[
    \widehat{\mathrm{e}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}: \mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}} \rightarrow \widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}
    \]
    the canonical functor induced by precomposition with the homomorphism $\mathcal{S}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_0} \mathbb{C}$.
<!-- end defi-20 -->
<!-- lem-21: body_md -->
\label{lem: last lemma}
    The abelian monoid $[[\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G, B \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G]]_{\operatorname{gr}}$ is a group for all $A,B \in \mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.
<!-- end lem-21 -->
<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
This follows from an argument very similar to the argument given in the proof of \Cref{thm: spectral model of g eq k theory}.1. See \cite[Lemma 2.1]{HG} for more details.
<!-- end proof-78 -->
<!-- thm-16: body_md -->
\label{thm: final}
\hfill
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For all $A,B \in \mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, we have a natural isomorphism $\mathrm{E}^{G_2}_{\mathrm{class}}(\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A,B) \cong \widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B)$.
    \item We have an equivalence of additive, symmetric monoidal (for the graded maximal tensor product) categories \[
    \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{\mathrm{ex},0}^{G,\mathrm{sep}} \simeq \widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}.
    \]
    \item For ungraded $C^*$-algebras $A$ and $B$ in $\mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, we have a natural isomorphism \[\widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B) \cong \mathrm{E}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}(A,B).\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-16 -->
<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Assertion 1 follows immediately from \Cref{thm: Gen DL} and \Cref{lem: last lemma}, keeping in mind that $\hat{\mathcal{K}}_G$ is inner graded. Assertion 2 follows from \Cref{thm: hoKKex is Eclass} for the group $G \times C_2$ (with the monoidal structure being the graded maximal tensor product), Assertion 1, and \Cref{lem: KKANA cat}.5. Assertion 3 was shown in the context of our stable $\infty$-categories in \Cref{thm: higson email to johannes}. We are therefore done by Assertion 2.
<!-- end proof-79 -->
<!-- rem-33: body_md -->
\label{last rem}
    In light of the main result of \cite{THOASY}, we can rework the last two subsections with \emph{completely positive} asymptotic morphisms, and obtain that for all $A,B \in \mathsf G\widehat{\mathsf C}^{*}\!\mathsf{Alg}^{\mathrm{sep}}$,
    \[
    \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{\mathrm{se},0}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}(A,B) \cong [[\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G, B \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G]]_{\operatorname{gr}}^{\operatorname{cp}}.
    \]
    However, unlike the definition of $\widehat{\mathrm{E}}^{G}_{\mathrm{class}}$ (which on the face of it is by asymptotic morphisms), the definition of $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ is in terms of Kasparov cycles. Therefore to complete the circle of ideas, we would need to obtain a natural isomorphism
    \[
    \widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}(A,B) \cong [[\mathcal{S} \hat\otimes A \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G, B \hat\otimes \hat{\mathcal{K}}_G]]_{\operatorname{gr}}^{\operatorname{cp}}.
    \]
    It is not clear to the author how to get a (clean) natural map in either direction. The problem seems to be that completely positive asymptotic morphisms do not naturally arise in practical situations.

    Nevertheless, Meyer has proven using different methods in \cite[Section 7]{MEYER} the analogue of the first two assertions of \Cref{thm: final} for $\widehat{KK}_{\operatorname{Kas}}^{G,\operatorname{sep}}$, whence the analogue of Assertion 3 of \Cref{thm: final} for $\widehat{\mathrm{KK}}_{\mathrm{Kas}}^{G,\mathrm{sep}}$ also follows from \Cref{thm: higson email to johannes}.
<!-- end rem-33 -->
